eng: Many also of those who had believed came, confessing, and declaring their deeds.

lmp: Bèe magòr efa wowèe ce a m ba ŋgâa tʉ', a m vʉ̀ nè wap mŋwà' tʉ' a lɛ àbee, a too à bsii bèe wɛɛwɛ. A ka' bè' mbàa ce a m yuu mŋwà' anà àgho a yɛ enɛ à m ba mmalàr mntâ.
eng: Many of those who practiced magical arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all. They counted the price of them, and found it to be fifty thousand pieces of silver.

lmp: Yi ka' ba wa'a, nlâa Tata Jisòs yi du à ŋgòŋ nè ŋger-ŋwɛ̀.
eng: So the word of the Lord was growing and becoming mighty.

lmp: Buu ca à ka' koni wa'a, Pol à laa enɛ àde' e buu efa càa à ŋgôŋ Mɛ̀sɛ̀donìyà ba à ŋgôŋ Àkayà dù Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m ka'. E m ker laa enɛ̂, "M ka' du ba' àfo, m ku du à rla' Rum foŋ."
eng: Now after these things had ended, Paul determined in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.

lmp: E ka' làa wa'a, a tuu Timotì ba Ɛ̀rastòs ce a m ce jà' ye à li rfà', enɛ a du à ŋgôŋ Mɛ̀sɛ̀donìyà, a biishi yi à ŋgôŋ Ɛshà.
eng: Having sent into Macedonia two of those who served him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in Asia for a while.

lmp: À m ba à nfè' anà ku' ŋgɛ' à kɛ' àtu buu ce a m ce yɛ'ni kuu nduunjî Tatâ.
eng: About that time there arose no small stir concerning the Way.

lmp: Ŋwɛ̀ ntòo nlàa mò' à m ba a ce too ye enɛ Dɛ̀mitròs. E m ce gèe mʉ mndap nyʉ̂ bkɛ'kɛ' nè njɛ̀ɛ bco' mo' ce a m ce too enɛ Silvà, vi feesè ndap nyʉ̀ Àtɛmìs. Bèe ce a m ce fà' nè ye a m ce ye sɛ' enjep rfà' anà sê.
eng: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, who made silver shrines of Artemis, brought no little business to the craftsmen,

lmp: E m kɛ' wowèe a bèe ce a m ce gèe njɛ̀ɛ ntaa anà foŋ àbee, a laa nè wowèe enɛ̂, "Yà bèe, wèe rìŋ enɛ see ke yeŋger bòŋboŋ sê, njobè' lisèe rfà' ca.
eng: whom he gathered together, with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, you know that by this business we have our wealth.

lmp: To wee wèe foŋ à yɛ a ker yu' yuu ce ŋwɛ̀ ce a too enɛ Pol na ce gèe à rla' Ɛfɛsòs, ker ba à ŋgôŋ Ɛsìyà wɛɛwɛ. Byɛ anà à làa enɛ mnyʉ̀ ce bèe a kupshi kupshi yu lɛ mnyʉ̀ ka'. E gèe wa'a, a beesi mntee ese bèe magòr.
eng: You see and hear, that not at Ephesus alone, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away many people, saying that they are no gods, that are made with hands.

lmp: Yi ku ba ba enɛ ŋgɛ' be koni sèe tɛ lisèe rfà' ca li kwe ntaa ka', bèe a be kèr lòr ndap nyʉ̀ Àtɛmìs anà à yuu ka', tɛ nyʉ̀ ca seese ce bêe à ŋgôŋ Ɛshà wɛɛwɛ a ce cà'ni na, ker kʉti ba yì ce àde' bèe a yu'nì nè ye ka'."
eng: Not only is there danger that this our trade come into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be counted as nothing, and her majesty destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worships.

lmp: Wowèe a ka' yu' ca, ntee yi bep wowèe sê, wowèe a kɛ' a ce ghaa a ce làa enɛ̂, "Àtɛmìs ce à rla' Ɛfɛsòs yu nyʉ̂ ŋgòr."
eng: When they heard this they were filled with anger, and cried out, saying, Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!

lmp: Nfè' à m tuuse ka', ghaa yi ko' à rla' Ɛfɛsòs wɛɛwɛ. Bèe ca a m koo Gayòs ba Àristakòs a du àgho mbe mambe ŋgòr. Bèe a mmbaa ca a m ba bêe à ŋgôŋ Mɛ̀sɛ̀donìyà ce a m ce kar a Pol wèe.
eng: The whole city was filled with confusion, and they rushed with one accord into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul's companions in travel.

lmp: Pol à m ce kòŋ enɛ e du niŋ mbe mʉ̀ bèe anà, ŋgâa yɛ'ni buu Jisòs a kanì.
eng: When Paul wanted to enter in to the people, the disciples didn't allow him.

lmp: Bèe mô' à ŋgôŋ Ɛsìyà ce a m ba bkar Pôl, a m cep ntuu nè ye, a laa enɛ e fa mòo ka'.
eng: Certain also of the Asiarchs, being his friends, sent to him and begged him not to venture into the theater.

lmp: Bèe ce a m kaari anà a m jep, a ce ghaa a ce làa buu jɛɛ jɛ̀ɛ jɛɛ njobè' bèe magòr a m rìŋ yap yu mbùu ce wowèe a m vʉ̀ mbo ka'.
eng: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another, for the assembly was in confusion. Most of them didn't know why they had come together.

lmp: Jus a m dòori Àlɛ̀ksandà a tɛr kùntombì nè bèe, a laa nè ye enɛ e laa yuu. Àlɛ̀ksandà à naa bo mbekì enɛ bèe a cu nyaŋ tɛ e laa yuu.
eng: They brought Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. Alexander beckoned with his hand, and would have made a defense to the people.

lmp: Wowèe a ka' yɛ enɛ e yu ŋwɛ̀ Jûs, wowèe a ghaa àbee àmbò awà baa wa'a, a ce làa enɛ̂, "Àtɛmìs ce à rla' Ɛfɛsòs yu nyʉ̂ ŋgòr."
eng: But when they perceived that he was a Jew, all with one voice for a time of about two hours cried out, Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!

lmp: Ŋwɛ̀ nsaŋ ŋwà' ce à rla' ca à gee bèe wɛɛwɛ a cu nyaŋ, e laa enɛ̂, "Yà bêe à rla' Ɛfɛsòs, ŋwɛ̀ wɛɛwɛ riŋ enɛ rla' Ɛfɛsòs a rla' ce li ke kè'ni ndap nyʉ̀ Àtɛmìs ce yu nyʉ̂ ŋgòr, a ker ba rla' ce li ke kè'ni yuu ce yi m gwè embe bùu nà.
eng: When the town clerk had quieted the multitude, he said, You men of Ephesus, what man is there who doesn't know that the city of the Ephesians is temple keeper of the great goddess Artemis, and of the image which fell down from Zeus?

lmp: Àde' ŋwɛ̀ mò' mɛŋnì buu ca ka', banɛ ŋwɛ̀ mò' fa kèr fa ŋgɛ' ka'. Cu nè mʉnyaŋ.
eng: Seeing then that these things can't be denied, you ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rash.

lmp: Wèe à vʉ̀ nè bèe ca mbena ce àmbò wowèe a yɛ̀ɛ buu embe mndap nyʉ̀ ka', a laa yuu mo' bebep àmbò yìsèe nyʉ̀ ka'.
eng: For you have brought these men here, who are neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of your goddess.

lmp: Dɛ̀mitròs ba yi ŋgâa mfà' a ka' tʉr yuu mo' kuu ŋwɛ̀ mò', banɛ wowèe a riŋ enɛ bkor vi ku tɛɛ btoo, ŋgâa rsa' a ba àgho, banɛ wowèe a du mbo sa' wâp mnsa'.
eng: If therefore Demetrius and the craftsmen who are with him have a matter against anyone, the courts are open, and there are proconsuls. Let them press charges against one another.

lmp: Wèe à ka' ker tʉr yuu mo' ce wèe à ba làa, wèe laa ba mbe rcutè ce bèe ce a ce sa' rla' a kɛ'.
eng: But if you seek anything about other matters, it will be settled in the regular assembly.

lmp: Àmbò yi yu sè'ni na, àde' a ku koo sèe àtu ŋgɛ' ce e koni ntìni na. Yi ka' koni wa'a, sèe tʉr yuu à rlàa ka'."
eng: For indeed we are in danger of being accused concerning this day's riot, there being no cause. Concerning it, we wouldn't be able to give an account of this commotion.

lmp: E ka' mìsi, a laa bèe à da'sè a duse.
eng: When he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.

lmp: Bjep ca vi ka' mì, Pol à kɛ' ŋgâa yɛ'ni buu Jisòs a laa buu nè wowèe, a fa wowèe ŋger, a daasi wowèe, a nati a ce dù à ŋgôŋ Mɛ̀sɛ̀donìyà.
eng: After the uproar had ceased, Paul sent for the disciples, took leave of them, and departed to go into Macedonia.

lmp: E ka' ce jɛ̀r à ŋgòŋ anà a ce làa ku' buu nè bèe, a ce fa wowèe ŋger nè blàa anà. E ka' mìsi, a du à ŋgôŋ Grês,
eng: When he had gone through those parts, and had encouraged them with many words, he came into Greece.

lmp: a cu àfo à mŋwɛɛ btaar. E ka' ce tami nyor à rdù à ŋgôŋ Sirìyà, a yɛ enɛ Jus a cu mncʉ̀ à rkoo ye yʉ, e kwa'shì à rkʉti dù njî à ŋgôŋ Mɛ̀sɛ̀donìyà.
eng: When he had spent three months there, and a plot was made against him by Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he determined to return through Macedonia.

lmp: Bèe ce a m dù a Pol wèe à m ba Sòpatà, muu yì Pairûs à rla' Bɛ̀riyà, ba Àristakòs ba Sɛ̀kundûs à rla' Tɛ̀sàlonikà, ba Gayôs à rla' Dɛbè, ba Timotì, ba Tikikòs a Trôfimòs ce a m ba bêe à ŋgôŋ Ɛshà.
eng: These accompanied him as far as Asia: Sopater of Beroea; Aristarchus and Secundus of the Thessalonians; Gaius of Derbe; Timothy; and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia.

lmp: Wowèe a m dù entombì a du a tɛɛ wèr à rla' Trowàs.
eng: But these had gone ahead, and were waiting for us at Troas.

lmp: Mnòŋ ce a m ce ye brɛ̂d ce a lɛ̀ yes njo ka' vi ka' càa, wèr à niŋ mbe keŋ a lô à rla' Filèpâi, mnòŋ vi ka' bà' tâ, wèr à konì wowèe à rla' Trowàs, a cu àfo à mnòŋ sàambâ.
eng: We sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas in five days, where we stayed seven days.

lmp: À ka' ba à nòŋ entòmbì embe mʉ̀ ŋgàa, wèr a vʉ àbee à rye byee Nyʉ̀. Pol à fe'shì blâa Nyʉ̀, a fe'shi caar a ba' nè ntee tʉ' njobè' e m rìŋ enɛ tʉ̀' be raa tɛ e dû.
eng: On the first day of the week, when the disciples were gathered together to break bread, Paul talked with them, intending to depart on the next day, and continued his speech until midnight.

lmp: A m cʉ̀'shi ku' blâm, a tooshi mbe mʉ̀ ndap embekì mbe dì' ce wèr à m ba anà.
eng: There were many lights in the upper room where we were gathered together.

lmp: Muu nsùnsù mò' ce a m ce too enɛ Yutikòs à m cu mbe wendù. Pol à ka' fè'shi dùni gòr, e buumì, a ka' buumi bòŋboŋ sê, a gwe embe ndàp ce e m ba mbendù yî mbekì. A ka' nàa ye mbekì e banì kwe.
eng: A certain young man named Eutychus sat in the window, weighed down with deep sleep. As Paul spoke still longer, being weighed down by his sleep, he fell down from the third story, and was taken up dead.

lmp: Pol à suu njep nshè a gwe mbe yê ndù, a baa ye nje nyòr, a laa enɛ̂, "Wèe fa wɛp ka', e ku bii ntèe."
eng: Paul went down, and fell upon him, and embracing him said, Don't be troubled, for his life is in him.

lmp: E ka' gèe wa'a, a kʉti mbe dì' ce e ba ba, a bɛ' brɛ̂d a ye, a de' a wowèe, caar tʉ̀' à râa. Tʉ̀' à ka' raa, e ma'shì wowèe a dû.
eng: When he had gone up, and had broken bread, and eaten, and had talked with them a long while, even until break of day, he departed.

lmp: Wowèe a m lòr muu nsùnsù ca ntèe a du àgho, yap ntee yi fʉtè sê.
eng: They brought the boy in alive, and were greatly comforted.

lmp: Wèr à m nàti yer a du entòmbì, a du a niŋ mbe keŋ ŋgòr a du à rla' Asòs. Yi m ba enɛ wèr be bà' àfo koo Pol mbe keŋ. Pol à m sèesi a wowèe wa'a njobè' e m kòŋ à rdù àfo nè mkùu.
eng: But we who went ahead to the ship set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul aboard there, for he had so arranged, intending himself to go by land.

lmp: E ka' vʉ̀ koni wèr àfo, wèr à koo ye mbe keŋ wèr wowèe a du à rla' Mitilèn.
eng: When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard, and came to Mitylene.

lmp: Wèr à natì a ce dù, tʉ̀' à ka' raa wèr à ba' a ce yɛ rla' Kiyòs nje wêr cùu. Tʉ̀' mò' à ka' raa, wèr à ba' à rla' Samòs. Tʉ̀' mò' à ka' kèr raa wèr à ba' à rla' Milɛtòs.
eng: Sailing from there, we came the following day opposite Chios. The next day we touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after we came to Miletus.

lmp: Pol à m yɛ enɛ e be tɛɛ à rla' Ɛfɛsòs ka', fà dì' e bo càasi nfè' mò' à ŋgôŋ Ɛshà ka', njobè' e m ce kòŋ enɛ e du cɛrcɛr tɛ e bo yɛ enɛ àde' e ba' à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m à nòŋ Pɛntikòs lɛ.
eng: For Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus, that he might not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hastening, if it were possible for him, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.

lmp: Pol à ka' bà' à rla' Milɛtòs, a cep ntuu enɛ btu embe cor à rla' Ɛfɛsòs a vʉ yɛ ye.
eng: From Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called to himself the elders of the assembly.

lmp: Wowèe a ka' vʉ̀ bà', Pol à laa nè wowèe enɛ̂, "Wèe rìŋ njɛ̀ɛ njì ce mɛ̀ m cu a wêe mʉ kɛ̂' à nòŋ ce mɛ̀ m tɛr kùu à ŋgôŋ Ɛshà.
eng: When they had come to him, he said to them, You yourselves know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, how I was with you all the time,

lmp: Mɛ̀ m ce fà' nè Tatâ, a ce nàa tu ka', a ce fà' nè mŋgoommir-ŋwɛ̀, ker ba mmòoshì ce mi m vʉ̀ nè mɛ̀ njo' mncʉ̀ ce Jus a m cʉ̀ mɛ̀.
eng: serving the Lord with all humility, with many tears, and with trials which happened to me by the plots of the Jews;

lmp: Wèe rìŋ enɛ mɛ̀ m buu efa rsuŋ wèe yuu mo' ce àde' wèe à m ba ye sɛ' enjo ka'. Mɛ̀ m ce fè'shi, a ker ce yɛ'ni wèe à mʉ̀ bèe ker ba à mndàp.
eng: how I didn't shrink from declaring to you anything that was profitable, teaching you publicly and from house to house,

lmp: Mɛ̀ m ce làa nè Jus ker ba bèe enje jɛɛ tatap se enɛ a kupse, ma' yàp buu bbebep, kʉti à mbèp yì Nyʉ̀, byemi nè Tata Jisòs.
eng: testifying both to Jews and to Greeks repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus.

lmp: "M ce dù à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m sè'ni na àmbò Yʉ' Rara yi làa enɛ m dû, a ke' riŋ yuu ce yi be dù koni mɛ̀ àfo ka'.
eng: Now, behold, I go bound by the Spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there;

lmp: Yuu mɛ̀ rìŋ cà'cà' yi yu enɛ Yʉ' Rara yi ce suŋ mɛ̀ à bbu' mla' wɛɛwɛ ce m ce dù enɛ m be dù shaŋ, kèr yɛ ŋgɛ'.
eng: except that the Holy Spirit testifies in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions wait for me.

lmp: Ka' yi yu wa'a, m ce lòr la ryòŋ àmbò ku' yuu mo' se ka', ku ba ba enɛ m du gee rfà' ce Tata Jisòs à m fa nè mɛ̀. Rfà' anà li yu enɛ m suŋ bèe Nsuŋ Mbòŋmboŋ àmbò ntee bòŋboŋ ce Nyʉ̀ tʉr nè bèe.
eng: But these things don't count; nor do I hold my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my race with joy, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to fully testify to the Good News of the grace of God.

lmp: "Mɛ̀ m jɛ̀r fa wêe mʉ a ce fè'shi àmbò kʉʉ Nyʉ̀. M rìŋ sè'ni na mɛnɛ àde' mò' efa wèe ker yɛ mɛ̀ ka'.
eng: Now, behold, I know that you all, among whom I went about preaching the Kingdom of God, will see my face no more.

lmp: E ka' làa wa' mìsi, a wowèe a gʉ'shì nè mŋkʉʉshi, e gee rloo.
eng: When he had spoken these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.

lmp: Wowèe a warsè sê, a baa ye nje nyòr nè ntee-ŋwɛ̀.
eng: They all wept a lot, and fell on Paul's neck and kissed him,

lmp: Yuu ce yi m gèe wowèe a koosìmnse sê, à m ba blàa ce e m làa enɛ wowèe a be kèr yɛ ye ka' nà. A wowèe a m dù a ba' àgee keŋ ŋgòr.
eng: sorrowing most of all because of the word which he had spoken, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him to the ship.

lmp: Wèr Pol wèe à ka' mà'shi wowèe, a niŋ mbe keŋ a du a ba' à rla' Kôs, a tɛɛ à dì' mo' ka'. Tʉ̀' à ka' raa wèr à ba' à rla' Rodòn, a ka' lô àfo, a du a ba' à rlà' Patarà.
eng: When it happened that we had parted from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

lmp: Wèr à ka' yɛ keŋ ce e m ce dù à rla' Fònishà, wèr à niŋ mbo a dû.
eng: Having found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard, and set sail.

lmp: Wèr à ka' bà' mbe dì' mo' yɛ rla' Saipròs, a ma'shi li à bo ŋkòp a caa a du a ba' à ŋgôŋ Sirìyà. Keŋ à du a tɛɛ à rla' Tayà tɛ a bo fʉshi buu embo àfo.
eng: When we had come in sight of Cyprus, leaving it on the left hand, we sailed to Syria, and landed at Tyre, for there the ship was to unload her cargo.

lmp: Wèr à du a yɛ ŋgâa yɛ'ni buu Jisòs àfo a cu wèr wowèe à mnòŋ sàambâ. Wowèe a m làa nè Pol à ŋger Yʉ' Rara enɛ e fa dù à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m ka'.
eng: Having found disciples, we stayed there seven days. These said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.

lmp: Geewa'a, yèr nfè' rdù à ka' ghɛɛ, wèr à natì a ce dù. Wowèe wɛɛwɛ ba wap bbyèŋge ba boo wap a m fʉʉ efa lap rla' ca a du wèr wowèe. Wèr wowèe à ka' bà' àwâa rò, a gʉ'shi nè mŋkʉʉshi a loo,
eng: When it happened that we had accomplished the days, we departed and went on our journey. They all, with wives and children, brought us on our way until we were out of the city. Kneeling down on the beach, we prayed.

lmp: a ma'shi mnyor. Wèr à niŋ mbe keŋ, wowèe a natì a kʉti.
eng: After saying goodbye to each other, we went on board the ship, and they returned home again.

lmp: Wèr à lô à rla' Tayà a du a ba' à rla' Tòlemɛ̀s, a ca'ni bfʉr vî àfo, a cu wèr wowèe à nôŋ mo'sir.
eng: When we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais. We greeted the brothers, and stayed with them one day.

lmp: Tʉ̀' à ka' raa, wèr à natì a du a ba' à rla' Sisàriyà, a niŋ mbe ndàp Felep ce e m ba ŋwɛ̀ rfè'shi Nsuŋ Mbòŋmboŋ, a cu wèr wowèe. E m ba mò' efa bèe nsàamba ce cor à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m à m ce nà.
eng: On the next day, we, who were Paul's companions, departed, and came to Caesarea. We entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.

lmp: E m tʉr boo bbyèŋge kyèe ce a m ce cep ntuu Nyʉ̀ nè bèe. Boo ca a m dù bgùu ka'.
eng: Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.

lmp: Wèr à ka' cu àfo à mʉ mnôŋ mo', ŋwɛ̀ ncep ntuu Nyʉ̀ ce a m ce too enɛ Àgabòs à vʉ̂ à ŋgôŋ Jùdiyà.
eng: As we stayed there some days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

lmp: E ka' vʉ̀ yɛ wèr, a fyɛɛ muu cɛ̀' ce Pol à m cʉʉ nje bʉ', a cʉʉ mi mkùu ba mi mkoo àgho, a laa enɛ̂, "Yʉ' Rara yi làa enɛ Jus à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m a be kur ŋwɛ̀ ce e tʉr muu cɛ̀' ca à njɛ̂ɛ wa'a, fa ye nè bèe enje jɛɛ."
eng: Coming to us, and taking Paul's belt, he bound his own feet and hands, and said, Thus says the Holy Spirit: 'So will the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man who owns this belt, and will deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.'

lmp: Wèr à ka' yu' wa'a, wèr bêe à rla' anà wèe à bu' mmbo nè ye enɛ e fa dù à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m ka'.
eng: When we heard these things, both we and they of that place begged him not to go up to Jerusalem.

lmp: Pol à laa enɛ̂, "Wèe ce war a ce koosi mɛ̀ bsɛ̀ wa'a njokɛ? Mɛ̀ ku tami nyor ba enɛ a koo mɛ̀ kur kur cà'cà' ka', mɛ̀ tami nyor foŋ à rkwe à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m àtu Tata Jisòs."
eng: Then Paul answered, What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.

lmp: E ka' kani yuu ce wèr à m làa, wèr à bornì yer yu, a laa wernɛ̂, "Tɛ Tata Nyʉ̀ gee yuu ce e kòŋ."
eng: When he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The Lord's will be done.

lmp: Mʉ mnòŋ vi ka' càa, wèr à kur buu a du à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m.
eng: After these days we took up our baggage and went up to Jerusalem.

lmp: Bèe mo' efa ŋgâa yɛ'ni buu Jisôs à rla' Sisàriyà anà a du wèr wowèe, a lor wèr a du àgho mbe ndàp Nasìn ce e m ba ŋwɛ̂ à ŋgôŋ Saipròs. A ŋwɛ̀ ce wèr à m ce dù à rcu wèr wowèe. E m ba mò' efa bèe entombì ce a m byemi nè Jisòs.
eng: Some of the disciples from Caesarea also went with us, bringing one Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we would stay.

lmp: Wèr à ka' bà' à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m, bfʉr ce a m ba àfo a konì wèr bòŋboŋ sê.
eng: When we had come to Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.

lmp: Tʉ̀' à ka' raa, wèr Pol wèe à du à ryɛ Jɛ̂ms, a ka' bà' a yɛ btu embe cor wɛɛwɛ a Jɛms wèe mbe dî' mo'sir.
eng: The day following, Paul went in with us to James; and all the elders were present.

lmp: Pol à ca'nì wowèe, a suŋ wowèe buu wɛɛwɛ ce Nyʉ̀ à gèe nè bèe enje jɛɛ njo' rfà' ce e m gèe fa wâp mʉ.
eng: When he had greeted them, he reported one by one the things which God had worked among the Gentiles through his ministry.

lmp: Wowèe a ka' yu', a ku'si Nyʉ̀, a laa nè Pol enɛ̂, "Nfʉ̂r, wɛ̀ yɛ àmbò Jus ce a byemi a yu à mncʉ̀kì à mncʉ̀kì, wowèe wɛɛwɛ a tʉr ntee à rlɛ̀ ncir sê.
eng: They, when they heard it, glorified God. They said to him, You see, brother, how many thousands there are among the Jews of those who have believed, and they are all zealous for the law.

lmp: Bèe a suŋ wowèe enɛ a ce yɛ'ni Jus ce a ce cu à bto' bèe enje jɛɛ enɛ wowèe a fa lɛ̀ mncir Musìs ka', a ce làa nè wowèe enɛ wowèe a fa gèe bʉ̀ ese boo ka', ma' lɛ ndèe to' foŋ.
eng: They have been informed about you, that you teach all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children neither to walk after the customs.

lmp: Àmbò yi yu na, banɛ sèe be gèe seekɛ? Wowèe a be buu efa ryu' enɛ wèe à vʉ̀ ka'.
eng: What then? The assembly must certainly meet, for they will hear that you have come.

lmp: Banɛ à gee yuu ce wèr be suŋ wɛ̀. Wèr tʉr bèe mò' bèe ŋkyèe ce a ye lè' nè Nyʉ̀.
eng: Therefore do what we tell you. We have four men who have taken a vow.

lmp: Lòr nè bèe ca tɛ wèe wowèe du gèe yuu ce ncir yi ce làa enɛ ŋwɛ̀ gee tɛ e bo ba nrara à bsii Nyʉ̀. Fa wowèe mbàa tɛ wowèe a bo koo btu. Wɛ̀ ka' gee wa'a, tɛ ŋwɛ̀ wɛɛwɛ bo rìŋ enɛ buu ce bèe a suŋ àmbò wɛ̀ nà, vi yu mini ka', rìŋ sè'ni enɛ wɛ wɛ̀ foŋ ce lɛ̀ mncir Musìs.
eng: Take them, and purify yourself with them, and pay their expenses for them, that they may shave their heads. Then all will know that there is no truth in the things that they have been informed about you, but that you yourself also walk keeping the law.

lmp: À ka' ba yi àmbò bèe enje jɛɛ ce a byemi, wèr à saŋ ŋwà' nè wowèe a suŋ yuu ce wèr à cu àbee a lâa. Wèr à làa wernɛ wowèe a fa ye byee ce a fa nè mnyʉ̀ enjep ŋgòŋ na ka', borni efa rye blɛɛ ba mnyàa ce a toosi mndoŋ efa gho, borni bsàkì."
eng: But concerning the Gentiles who believe, we have written our decision that they should observe no such thing, except that they should keep themselves from food offered to idols, from blood, from strangled things, and from sexual immorality.

lmp: Tʉ̀' à ka' raa, Pol à lor bèe anà a wowèe a gee yuu ce ncir yi m ce làa enɛ a gee tɛ a bo ba brara à bsii Nyʉ̀. A wowèe a ka' mìsi, e du mbe Ndàp Nyʉ̀, a suŋ bèe nòŋ ce wowèe a be gèe buu anà mìsi tɛ a bo vʉ̀ fa rfa àtu ŋwɛ̀ wɛɛwɛ.
eng: Then Paul took the men, and the next day, purified himself and went with them into the temple, declaring the fulfillment of the days of purification, until the offering was offered for every one of them.

lmp: Mnòŋ sàamba ca vi ka' kɛ̀' ce mì, Jus mô' à ŋgôŋ Ɛshà à yɛ Pol mbe Ndàp Nyʉ̀. Wowèe a ka' yɛ ye mbo, a barsi bèe fa yê mbùu, a wowèe a koo ye,
eng: When the seven days were almost completed, the Jews from Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the multitude and laid hands on him,

lmp: a waa enɛ̂, "Bèe Isrɛ̀l, jà' nè wèr! Ŋwɛ̀ ca a ŋwɛ̀ ce e ce jɛ̀r ce yɛ'ni bèe wɛɛwɛ enɛ yìsèe bèe ba visèe mncir ker ba yìsèe Ndap Nyʉ̀ ca yu yuu ka'. E ker lor bèe enje jɛɛ foŋ a niŋ àgho mbe Ndàp Nyʉ̀, a bepsi dî' rara ca yi ba jàpri."
eng: crying out, Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches all men everywhere against the people, and the law, and this place. Moreover, he also brought Greeks into the temple, and has defiled this holy place!

lmp: Wowèe a m làa wa'a njobè' a m yɛ Trôfimòs ce à rla' Ɛfɛsòs a Pol wèe à rla' anà, a ce kwà'shi enɛ Pol à m lòr ye a du àgho mbe Ndàp Nyʉ̀.
eng: For they had seen Trophimus, the Ephesian, with him in the city, and they supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.

lmp: Rla' wɛɛwɛ li ci'tì, bèe a caŋsè a vʉse a koo Pôl, a sʉŋ a fʉʉ àgho embe Ndàp Nyʉ̀, a cete ncʉ̀ʉndʉ̀',
eng: All the city was moved, and the people ran together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Immediately the doors were shut.

lmp: a ce ghèter à ryʉ ye. Nsuŋ à vʉ a ba' ŋwɛ̀ ce e m ba tu nè bsoogɛ̀ ncʉ̀kì enɛ rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m wɛɛwɛ li jep.
eng: As they were trying to kill him, news came up to the commanding officer of the regiment that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

lmp: E lor bsoogɛ̀ mo' ba btu mo' a wowèe a caŋ a du a yɛ ku' kʉr bèe anà. Wowèe a ka' yɛ a bsoogɛ̀ wèe, a borni efa rlìp Pôl.
eng: Immediately he took soldiers and centurions, and ran down to them. They, when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, stopped beating Paul.

lmp: Tu bsoogɛ̀ yî gòr ca à m koo Pôl, a laa enɛ a kur ye nè bshaŋ bbaa, a bipshi nè bèe enɛ Pol yu nda lɛ, a ker bipshi enɛ e gèe ba kɛ lɛ?
eng: Then the commanding officer came near, arrested him, commanded him to be bound with two chains, and inquired who he was and what he had done.

lmp: Bèe mo' efa mʉ̀ kʉr bèe ca a m làa yuu jɛɛ, bèe mo' a laa yuu jɛɛ. Bjep vi ba gòr sê, yi ba àtɛ̀r nè ye à rrìŋ yuu ce yi koni ka', e laa enɛ a lor Pol du àgho mbe barakì.
eng: Some shouted one thing, and some another, among the crowd. When he couldn't find out the truth because of the noise, he commanded him to be brought into the barracks.

lmp: Pol à ka' bà' mbe dì' ce a be lò embo ce ko' ko', bèe a gʉmì a yê ndù, bsoogɛ̀ a boŋlàr a byɛ' ye.
eng: When he came to the stairs, it happened that he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd;

lmp: Kʉr bèe ca a m ce dù a yê mbùu a ce ghaa a ce làa enɛ̂, "Yʉ nè ye!"
eng: for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, Away with him!

lmp: A ka' koo Pol tɛ a bo niŋ àgho mbe barakì, e laa nè ŋwɛ̀ ce e m ba tu bsoogɛ̀ yî gòr ca nà enɛ̂, "Àde' m laa yuu a?" E beesì enɛ̂, "Banɛ wɛ̂ ke làa li Grêk a?
eng: As Paul was about to be brought into the barracks, he asked the commanding officer, May I speak to you? He said, Do you know Greek?

lmp: Mbò a wɛ̀ ŋwɛ̂ à to' Ijìp ce e m kɛ̀' ŋgɛ', a lor ŋgâa nyʉshi bèe ncʉ̀kì kyèe à nfè' mò' a du àgho à ntee rìŋ nà a?"
eng: Aren't you then the Egyptian, who before these days stirred up to sedition and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?

lmp: Pol à beesì enɛ̂, "M yu ŋwɛ̀ Jus ce à rla' Tasôs à ŋgôŋ Sìlesìyà ce yu rla' ce li yu àtɛ̀r ka'. Kyer wɛ̀, mà'shi tɛ m laa yuu nè bèe ca."
eng: But Paul said, I am a Jew, from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city. I beg you, allow me to speak to the people.

lmp: Ŋwɛ̀ anà à ma'shì enɛ e lâa. Pol à tɛɛ mbe dì' ce e m ko' a tɛɛ nà, a naa bo mbekì enɛ bèe a cu nyaŋ. Bèe a ka' cu nyaŋ, e laa nè wowèe à li Hibrù enɛ̂,
eng: When he had given him permission, Paul, standing on the stairs, beckoned with his hand to the people. When there was a great silence, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, saying,

lmp: "Yà bèe, bfʉr wâ, ba yà ta wèe, yu' nè yuu ce e m be làa."
eng: Brothers and fathers, listen to the defense which I now make to you.

lmp: Wowèe a ka' yu' àmbò e làa nè wowèe ba à li Hibrù, wowèe a misì a cu nyòŋ. Pol à laa enɛ̂,
eng: When they heard that he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, they were even more quiet. He said,

lmp: "M yu ŋwɛ̀ Jus ce a m bi ba à rla' Tasòs à ŋgôŋ Sìlesìyà. Geewa'a, mɛ̀ m kù' à rlâ' àfa na. Mɛ̀ m cu njeptii Gàmalìyàl, e yɛ'nì mɛ̀ mncir visèe btarkʉ bòŋboŋ sê, ya ntee yi ce lùu mɛ̀ à rdù àmbùu Nyʉ̀ àmbò ye foŋ yi ce lùu ntìni na."
eng: I am indeed a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to the strict tradition of the law of our fathers, being zealous for God, even as you all are this day.

lmp: Mɛ̀ laa mɛnɛ̂, "M be gèe mɛ kɛ Tatâ?" Tata à beesì enɛ̂, "Nàti mbekì du à rla' Dàmaskòs. À be bà' àfo tɛ a suŋ wɛ̀ buu wɛɛwɛ ce Tàr à ce enɛ à gêe."
eng: I said, 'What shall I do, Lord?' The Lord said to me, 'Arise, and go into Damascus. There you will be told about all things which are appointed for you to do.'

lmp: Rraa ce li m raa nà li m niŋ mɛ̀ njep mmìr, mɛ̀ fêp, bèe ce wèr wowèe à m ba a koo mɛ̀ à bò a du àgho à rla' Dàmaskòs.
eng: When I couldn't see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of those who were with me, I came into Damascus.

lmp: "Ŋwɛ̀ mò' ce a m ce too enɛ Ànàniyàs à m ba à rla' anà, à ba ŋwɛ̀ ce e m ce lɛ̀ mncir yɛɛnì sê. Jus àfo wɛɛwɛ a m ce làa bòŋboŋ àmbò ye sê.
eng: One Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well reported of by all the Jews who lived in Damascus,

lmp: E m vʉ̀ a yɛ mɛ̀, a tɛɛ a mɛ̂ geŋ a laa enɛ̂, "Nfʉrâ Sôl, yɛ buu." Mɛ̀ yɛ buu à nfè' anà, a yɛ ye àmbò e tɛɛ.
eng: came to me, and standing by me said to me, 'Brother Saul, receive your sight!' In that very hour I looked up at him.

lmp: E laa enɛ̂, "Nyʉ̀ yì visèe btarkʉ à ce wɛ̀ tɛ à bo rìŋ yuu ce e ce kòŋ enɛ à gêe, kèr yɛ yì Ŋwɛ̀ Rfâ' Nyɛɛnì, yu' àmbò e ce làa,
eng: He said, 'The God of our fathers has appointed you to know his will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from his mouth.

lmp: njobè' à be ba yì ŋwɛ̀ ce à be suŋ bèe wɛɛwɛ buu ce wɛ̀ yɛ a ker yu'.
eng: For you will be a witness for him to all men of what you have seen and heard.

lmp: À ker ce kè' ba kɛ sè'ni? Nàti mbekì, kɛ' li rlii, tɛ a baptir wɛ̀, sù'si yò buu bebep."
eng: Now why do you wait? Arise, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.'

lmp: "Mɛ̀ ka' kʉti à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m ce gèe rloo mbe Ndàp Nyʉ̀, a yɛ njɛ̀ɛ rlo mo'.
eng: It happened that, when I had returned to Jerusalem, and while I prayed in the temple, I fell into a trance,

lmp: Pol à m ce làa bèe a ku ce yu'shi, e ka' ce làa àmbò bèe enje jɛɛ, wowèe a ghâa, a laa enɛ̂, "Wèe fa mà'shi ye ka', yʉ nè ye."
eng: They listened to him until he said that; then they lifted up their voice, and said, Rid the earth of this fellow, for he isn't fit to live!

lmp: Wowèe a ce ghaa, a co'ni wap bcɛ̀' a ce mà'ri, ce dʉ'si nfʉ̀nfʉ mbekì.
eng: As they cried out, and threw off their cloaks, and threw dust into the air,

lmp: Ŋwɛ̀ ce e m ba tu nà à laa enɛ a lor Pol niŋ àgho mbe barakì, lip ye, bipshi buu nè ye tɛ a bo rìŋ mbùu ce Jus a m ce ghaa ye à njɛ̂ɛ wa'a.
eng: the commanding officer commanded him to be brought into the barracks, ordering him to be examined by scourging, that he might know for what crime they shouted against him like that.

lmp: Wowèe a kur ye tɛ a bo lìp, e laa nè ŋwɛ̀ ce e m ba tu nè bsoogɛ̀ rjèe enɛ̂, "Wà' ncir yi byemi enɛ a lip ŋwɛ̀ Rum ce a be sa' yì nsa' ka' a?"
eng: When they had tied him up with thongs, Paul asked the centurion who stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman, and not found guilty?

lmp: Ŋwɛ̀ ce e m ba tu nè bsoogɛ̀ rjèe nà à ka' yu' ca, a du a suŋ nè tu yî gòr. E m làa nè ye enɛ̂, "À be gèe wɛkɛ sè'ni à? Ŋwɛ̀ ca yu ŋwɛ̀ Rûm."
eng: When the centurion heard it, he went to the commanding officer and told him, Watch what you are about to do, for this man is a Roman!

lmp: Tu yî gòr yi du a yɛ Pôl, a bipshi nè ye enɛ̂, "Suŋ ka mɛ̀ lɛ̂, à yu ŋwɛ̀ Rum a?" E beesì enɛ ɛ̀no.
eng: The commanding officer came and asked him, Tell me, are you a Roman? He said, Yes.

lmp: Tu ca yi laa nè ye enɛ̂, "Mɛ̀ m là' ku' mbàa gòr sê, ka' ba ŋwɛ̀ Rûm." Pol à laa enɛ̂, "A m bi yi mɛ̀ à ŋwɛ̀ Rûm."
eng: The commanding officer answered, I bought my citizenship for a great price. Paul said, But I was born a Roman.

lmp: Bèe ce a m ba enɛ a be bipshi buu nè ye nà, a natì a tɛɛ encàŋ. Tu yî gòr foŋ yi m lò a wɛp à nfè' ce e m rìŋ enɛ e koo Pol ce yu ŋwɛ̀ Rûm, a kur.
eng: Immediately those who were about to examine him departed from him, and the commanding officer also was afraid when he realized that he was a Roman, because he had bound him.

lmp: Tu yî gòr yi m ce kòŋ à rrìŋ rara enɛ Jus ca a m ce làa enɛ Pol à gèe ba kɛ lɛ. Tʉ̀' à ka' raa, e ba'shì ye efa bshaŋ, a laa bêe bgòrgòr efa mʉ̀ ŋgâa taŋshi taŋshì ba ŋgâa kansùr wɛɛwɛ a vʉsè. E vʉ nè Pol a tɛr mbe kansùr.
eng: But on the next day, desiring to know the truth about why he was accused by the Jews, he freed him from the bonds, and commanded the chief priests and all the council to come together, and brought Paul down and set him before them.

lmp: Pol à fyɛ' ŋgâa kansùr enɛ ntuŋ-ŋ-ŋ, a laa enɛ̂, "Yà bèe, mɛ̀ cu la rcu vʉ ba' ntìni na nè ntee rara-ŋwɛ̀ à bsii Nyʉ̀."
eng: Paul, looking steadfastly at the council, said, Brothers, I have lived before God in all good conscience until this day.

lmp: Tu ŋgâa taŋshi taŋshì ce a n ce too enɛ Ànàniyàs à laa nè bèe ce a m tɛɛ àgee Pol enɛ wowèe a lip ye à cùu.
eng: The high priest, Ananias, commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.

lmp: Pol à laa nè ye enɛ̂, "Nyʉ̀ be lìp wɛ̀, wɛ̀ ce à yu àmbò ŋgʉ̀' ndap mbʉʉ. Wɛ̀ lòr mncir a ce sa' mɛ̀ àgho, a ker ce bʉ' mncir anà njobè' wɛ̀ làa enɛ a lip mɛ̀."
eng: Then Paul said to him, God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! Do you sit to judge me according to the law, and command me to be struck contrary to the law?

lmp: Bèe ce a m tɛɛ àgee Pol, a laa nè ye enɛ̂, "À ce cɛp tu ŋgâa taŋshi taŋshì yî Nyʉ̀ a?"
eng: Those who stood by said, Do you malign God's high priest?

lmp: Pol à beesì enɛ̂, "Bfʉr wâ, mɛ̀ ba riŋ enɛ a tu ŋgâa taŋshi taŋshì ka'. A saŋ mbe Ŋwâ' Nyʉ̀ enɛ̂, "Fa làa yuu bebep kùu ŋwɛ̀ ce e ce sa' yò bèe ka'." "
eng: Paul said, I didn't know, brothers, that he was high priest. For it is written, 'You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.'

lmp: Pol à m rìŋ enɛ bèe mo' embe kansùr a yu Sadùsî, bèe mo' a ba Farìsî, a laa nè ŋgâa kansùr enɛ̂, "Yà bèe, m yu ŋwɛ̀ Farìsî, a ba muu ŋwɛ̀ Farìsî. M tɛɛ mbe kansùr na à mnsa' njo' m ce kè' enɛ bèe ce a kweŋger a be kè fʉʉ efa rkwe."
eng: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged!

lmp: E ka' làa wa'a, bèe Farìsi ba bèe Sadùsi a kɛ' a ce lapni, a fʉʉ nto' baa.
eng: When he had said this, an argument arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.

lmp: Bèe Sadùsi a kani enɛ nfʉʉ-efa-rkwe yu àgho ka', a ker kani enɛ bcìndap Nyʉ̀ ker ba byʉ' vi yu àgho ka'. Bèe Farìsi a byemì enɛ buu ca wɛɛwɛ yu àgho.
eng: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess all of these.

lmp: Bèe a misì a ghaa gòr sê, bèe mo' efa ŋgâa ryɛ'ni mncir ce a m ba yap bèe Farìsî, a natì mbekì a laa tatap sê, enɛ̂, Wèr a yɛ fàa mò' nè ŋwɛ̀ ca ka'! Sèe rìŋ nè kɛ àmbò à làa ba yʉ' mo' kɛ̀ ncìndap Nyʉ̀ nè ye.
eng: A great clamor arose, and some of the scribes of the Pharisees part stood up, and contended, saying, We find no evil in this man. But if a spirit or angel has spoken to him, let's not fight against God!

lmp: Bèe a lapnì gòr sê, tu yî gòr yi wɛp enɛ a be koo Pol sàsi. E laa nè bsoogɛ̀ enɛ wowèe a du koo ye à ŋger niŋ àgho mbe barakì.
eng: When a great argument arose, the commanding officer, fearing that Paul would be torn in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force from among them, and bring him into the barracks.

lmp: Tʉ̀' à ka' sii, Tata Jisòs à vʉ a tɛɛ àgee Pôl, a laa nè ye enɛ̂, "Tɛɛ tatap, fa wɛp ka'! Wɛ̀ suŋ bèe àmbò mɛ̀ à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m, à be dù suŋ bèe àmbò mɛ̀ foŋ à rla' Rûm."
eng: The following night, the Lord stood by him, and said, Cheer up, Paul, for as you have testified about me at Jerusalem, so you must testify also at Rome.

lmp: Tʉ̀' à ka' raa, Jus mo' a cutè a ye lè' enɛ wowèe a ka' tɛ yʉ Pol ka' wowèe a ye yuu ka', ker no yuu ka'.
eng: When it was day, some of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.

lmp: Bèe ce a m ye lè' ca a m càa bèe mkyèe.
eng: There were more than forty people who had made this conspiracy.

lmp: Wowèe a du a yɛ bêe bgòrgòr efa mʉ̀ ŋgâa taŋshi taŋshì ba bleebèe, a laa nè wowèe enɛ̂, "Wèr à ye lè' tatap sê, enɛ wèr à ka' tɛ yʉ Pol ka' wèr joo yuu kù cùu ka'.
eng: They came to the chief priests and the elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.

lmp: Banɛ wèe kansùr wèe à ba cep ntuu nè tu yî gòr enɛ e vʉ nè Pol fa nè wèe, àmbò wèe ce lɛ kòŋ à rfyɛ' njep mʉ̀ vi mnsa' bòŋboŋ wa'a. Wèr à tami nyor à ryʉ ye tɛ e ka' vʉ̀ bà'."
eng: Now therefore, you with the council inform the commanding officer that he should bring him down to you tomorrow, as though you were going to judge his case more exactly. We are ready to kill him before he comes near.

lmp: Muu njar Pol à yu' mncʉ̀ ce wowèe a m cʉ̀ na, a du a niŋ mbe barakì a suŋ Pôl.
eng: But Paul's sister's son heard of their lying in wait, and he came and entered into the barracks and told Paul.

lmp: Pol à kɛ' tu mo', a laa nè ye enɛ̂, "Lòr muu nsùnsù ca du fa nè tu yî gòr, e ròo suŋ ye yuu mo'."
eng: Paul summoned one of the centurions, and said, Bring this young man to the commanding officer, for he has something to tell him.

lmp: E lor ye a du àgho a fa nè tu yî gòr, a laa nè ye enɛ̂, "Pol ce e yu ŋwɛ̀ shaŋ nà à kɛ' mɛ̀, a laa nè mɛ̀ enɛ m vʉ nè muu nsùnsù ca fa nè wɛ̀ njobè' e ròo suŋ wɛ̀ yuu mo'."
eng: So he took him, and brought him to the commanding officer, and said, Paul, the prisoner, summoned me and asked me to bring this young man to you, who has something to tell you.

lmp: Tu yî gòr yi koo ye à rkoo, a ye a lɛ'sì nyor, e bipshì nè ye enɛ̂, "Yuu ce wɛ̂ ròo suŋ mɛ̀ yu kɛ?"
eng: The commanding officer took him by the hand, and going aside, asked him privately, What is it that you have to tell me?

lmp: E laa enɛ̂, "Jus a cu a fa ntaŋ enɛ a be làa nè wɛ̀ enɛ à vʉ nè Pol mbe kansùr àyàŋsè àmbò wowèe a ce lɛ kòŋ à rniŋ njep mʉ̀ mnsa' ca bòŋboŋ wa'a.
eng: He said, The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though intending to inquire somewhat more accurately concerning him.

lmp: Fa byemi ka' njobè' bèe ce a càa bèe mkyèe a be tɛ' ye à nduunjì. Wowèe a ye lè' enɛ a ka' tɛ yʉ Pol ka', a ye yuu ka', ker no yuu ka'. Wowèe a tami nyor sè'ni a ce kè' enɛ à byemi gee yuu ce wowèe a be làa."
eng: Therefore don't yield to them, for more than forty men lie in wait for him, who have bound themselves under a curse neither to eat nor to drink until they have killed him. Now they are ready, looking for the promise from you.

lmp: Tu yî gòr yi laa nè ye enɛ e dû. E dù e fa suŋ ŋwɛ̀ mò' yuu ce e suŋ ye nà ka'.
eng: So the commanding officer let the young man go, charging him, Tell no one that you have revealed these things to me.

lmp: E m kɛ' btu mo' a baa ce a m ce fà' njep yê tìi, a laa nè wowèe enɛ̂, "Lòr nè bsoogɛ̀ mjêe mmbaa, ba ŋgâa mnyàabàrà' msàambâ, ba ŋgâa mkòŋ mjêe mmbaa tɛ wèe wowèe lo nètʉ' na à nyʉ̀ bʉ̀'ʉ̂, dù à rla' Sisàriyà.
eng: He called to himself two of the centurions, and said, Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, with seventy horsemen, and two hundred men armed with spears, at the third hour of the night.

lmp: Fyɛ' nè mnyàabàrà' mo' tɛ Pol cu mbo tɛ wèe lor ye dù àgho bòŋboŋ dù fa nè Fɛlìs ce e yu govanò."
eng: He asked them to provide animals, that they might set Paul on one, and bring him safely to Felix the governor.

lmp: Tu yî gòr yi saŋ ŋwà' foŋ enɛ̂,
eng: He wrote a letter like this:

lmp: "Ŋwà' ca à saŋ mɛ̂ Klâdìyòs Lesà nè wɛ̂ màsà Fɛlìs ce à yu govanò. Mɛ̀ cà'ni wɛ̀.
eng: Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.

lmp: Mɛ̀ koŋ à rrìŋ yuu ce a m làa enɛ e gèe, a lor ye a du àgho mbe yàp kansùr.
eng: Desiring to know the cause why they accused him, I brought him down to their council.

lmp: Mɛ̀ ka' dù nè ye mbo, a yɛ mɛnɛ e m gèe yuu mo' ce àde' a m ba yʉ ye kɛ̀ fa ye mbe shaŋ ka'. Yuu ce a m ce làa àmbò ye à m ba ba buu ce a m ce bipshi nè ye kuu yap ncir.
eng: I found him to be accused about questions of their law, but not to be charged with anything worthy of death or of imprisonment.

lmp: Ŋwɛ̀ à suŋ mɛ̀ enɛ Jus a cu mncʉ̀ enɛ a bo tɛ' ye, koo yʉ, mɛ̀ laa mɛnɛ a lor ye du àgho cɛrcɛr fa nè wɛ̀. Mɛ̀ ker laa foŋ nè bèe ce a m ce kòŋ à rsa' mnsa' a Pol nà enɛ wowèe a vʉ njep wɛ̂ tìi, suŋ yuu ce e gèe."
eng: When I was told that the Jews lay in wait for the man, I sent him to you immediately, charging his accusers also to bring their accusations against him before you. Farewell.

lmp: Bsoogɛ̀ a m ku gee àmbò a m làa nè wowèe, a lor Pol nètʉ', a du àgho a ba' à rla' Àntipàtidà.
eng: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.

lmp: Tʉ̀' à ka' raa, wowèe a kʉtì yap mbe barakì, ŋgâa mnyàabàrà' a du a Pol wèe.
eng: But on the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the barracks.

lmp: Wowèe a ka' dù bà' à rla' Sisàriyà, fa ŋwà' nè govanò wɛɛ, a fa Pol nè ye foŋ.
eng: When they came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.

lmp: Govanò à ka' bè' ŋwà' anà, a bipshi nè Pol enɛ a ye ŋwɛ̂ à ŋgòŋ efɛ lɛ? E ka' yu' enɛ e yu ŋwɛ̂ à ŋgôŋ Sìlesìyà,
eng: When the governor had read it, he asked what province he was from. When he understood that he was from Cilicia, he said,

lmp: a laa enɛ̂, "M be yu'shi wo mnsa' à nfè' ce bèe ce wèe wowèe à m ce sa' mnsa' mbe kansùr nà a vʉ̀ foŋ." E m làa enɛ a lor Pol du àgho mbe nto' Hɛròd ce ke'nî.
eng: I will hear you fully when your accusers also arrive. He commanded that he be kept in Herod's palace.

lmp: Mnòŋ vi ka' càa tâ, Ànàniyàs ce e m ba tu nè ŋgâa taŋshi taŋshì à lor bleebèe ba loyà mò' ce a m ce too enɛ Tɛ̀tulò, wowèe a du a suŋ govanò buu ce Pol à m gèe.
eng: After five days, the high priest, Ananias, came down with certain elders and an orator, one Tertullus. They informed the governor against Paul.

lmp: A kɛ' Pôl, e ka' vʉ̀, Tɛ̀tulò à kɛ' a ce suŋ govanò buu ce Pol à m gèe, a ce làa nè ye enɛ̂, "Wɛ̀ sa' wèr, wèr à cu nè cumʉnyaŋ-ŋwɛ̀ sê. À ka' ba njo' buu ce wɛ̀ gèe nè wèr, bdì' wɛɛwɛ efa yer ŋgòŋ vi ba yɛɛnì.
eng: When he was called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by you we enjoy much peace, and that excellent measures are coming to this nation,

lmp: Wèr à byemi yuu ce wɛ̀ gèe na à bdì' wɛɛwɛ ba à nfè' wɛɛwɛ, a ce yòŋshi wɛ̀ magòr sê.
eng: we accept it in all ways and in all places, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.

lmp: M ce kòŋ mɛnɛ m caasi yò nfè' ka', a ce bu' mmbo nè wɛ̀ enɛ à fa mʉ nfè' mò', yu' yuu ce wèr be suŋ wɛ̀.
eng: But, that I don't delay you, I entreat you to bear with us and hear a few words.

lmp: Wèr à yɛ ŋwɛ̀ ca à ba ŋwɛ̀ ŋgɛ' sê. E ce tèesi btu ese Jus à ŋgòŋ wɛɛwɛ, a ba tu mo' nè bèe ce a dà' enjep nduunjì Nyʉ̀ ce a too enɛ Nasarɛ̂n.
eng: For we have found this man to be a plague, an instigator of insurrections among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.

lmp: E m ghèter foŋ enɛ e gee tɛ Ndap Nyʉ̀ ba jàpri, wèr à koo ye.
eng: He even tried to profane the temple, and we arrested him.

lmp: Wɛ̀ ka' bipshi buu nè ye, wɛ wɛ̀ foŋ ku riŋ yuu ce yi yu mini kuu buu ce wèr à suŋ wɛ̀ enɛ e gèe na."
eng: By examining him yourself you may ascertain all these things of which we accuse him.

lmp: Jus a m bèe njì Tɛ̀tulò, a laa enɛ buu ce e làa vi yu mini.
eng: The Jews also joined in the attack, affirming that these things were so.

lmp: Govanò à naa bo enɛ Pol lâa, Pol à laa enɛ̂, "Mɛ̀ rìŋ mɛnɛ wɛ̀ sa' to' ca à bfè' àŋgoo, mɛ̀ ce lu'shi à rsuŋ yuu ce yi yu.
eng: When the governor had beckoned to him to speak, Paul answered, Because I know that you have been a judge of this nation for many years, I cheerfully make my defense,

lmp: Àde' wɛ wɛ̀ foŋ ku fyɛ' yɛ enɛ kɛ̂' nyʉ̀ ce mɛ̀ m dù à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m à rloo nè Nyʉ̀ vʉ ba' ntìni na, ku ba ba mnòŋ ncòp baa-à-rrʉ̀ʉ.
eng: seeing that you can recognize that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship at Jerusalem.

lmp: Jus a m yɛ mɛ̀ ce sɛr mnsɛr wèr ŋwɛ̀ mò' embe Ndàp Nyʉ̀ ka', a ker yɛ enɛ mɛ̀ ce kɛ̀' ŋgɛ' à mndàp mloo kɛ̀ à dì' mo' à rla' na ka'.
eng: In the temple they didn't find me disputing with anyone or stirring up a crowd, either in the synagogues, or in the city.

lmp: Àde' wowèe a duŋshì nè wɛ̀ enɛ buu ce a ce suŋ enɛ mɛ̀ gèe na vi yu mini ka'.
eng: Nor can they prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.

lmp: Yuu ce m ce byemi a wɛ̂ bsii yi yu enɛ, m ce loo Nyʉ̀ wêr bta à nduunjì mo' ce Jus a làa yap enɛ a nduunjî yɛɛnì ka'. Mɛ̀ byemi buu wɛɛwɛ ce a saŋ mbe ŋwâ' mncir ba mŋwâ' ŋgâa ncep ntuu Nyʉ̀.
eng: But this I confess to you, that after the Way, which they call a sect, so I serve the God of our fathers, believing all things which are according to the law, and which are written in the prophets;

lmp: Mɛ̀ byemi nè Nyʉ̀, a ce kè' àmbò wowèe foŋ a byemi a ce kè' enɛ bêe bbòŋboŋ ba bêe bbebep a be kè fʉʉ efa rkwe nà.
eng: having hope toward God, which these also themselves look for, that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.

lmp: Yi ka' ba wa'a, mɛ̀ ce ghèter sê, à rlɛ̀ ya ntee rara à nfè' wɛɛwɛ à bsii Nyʉ̀ ba ŋwɛ̀.
eng: Herein I also practice always having a conscience void of offense toward God and men.

lmp: "Bfè' mo' vi ka' càa, mɛ̀ lo a vʉ̂ a mɛ̂ to' tɛ m bo jà' ŋgâa ŋgɛ' nè mbàa, kèr fa rfa nè Nyʉ̀.
eng: Now after some years, I came to bring gifts for the needy to my nation, and offerings;

lmp: Mɛ̀ ka' ce gèe buu ca, wowèe a vʉ a yɛ mɛ̀ mbe Ndàp Nyʉ̀. Wowèe a m ce yɛ mɛ̀ wa'a, mɛ̀ gèe nè yuu ce ncir yi làa enɛ ŋwɛ̀ gee tɛ e bo ba rara à bsii Nyʉ̀ nà wɛɛ, a ba wèr kʉr bèe ka', ŋgɛ' mò' à ba ka'.
eng: amid which certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, not with a mob, nor with turmoil.

lmp: Ka' yi yu wa'a, Jus mô' à ŋgôŋ Ɛshà a m ba àfo. Wowèe a ba vʉ̀ tɛɛ a wɛ̂ bsii, làa yuu, ce yi ka' ba enɛ wowèe a tʉr yuu kuu mɛ̀.
eng: They ought to have been here before you, and to make accusation, if they had anything against me.

lmp: Ka' bèe ce a vʉ̀ na, a ba suŋ fàa ce mɛ̀ m gèe ka' kè tɛɛ mbe kansùr.
eng: Or else let these men themselves say what injustice they found in me when I stood before the council,

lmp: Ku ba yuu yi mo'sir ca ce mɛ̀ rìŋ mɛnɛ mɛ̀ m làa mbe kansùr: Mɛ̀ m làa mɛnɛ̂, "Mɛ̀ tɛɛ mbe kansùr ntìni na njobè' mɛ̀ byemi mɛnɛ bèe ce a kweŋger a be kè fʉʉ efa rkwe."
eng: unless it is for this one thing that I cried standing among them, 'Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged before you today!'

lmp: Fɛlìs ce e m rìŋ nduunjì anà bòŋboŋ sê, à ku' mnsa', a laa nè wowèe enɛ̂, "Lesà ce e yu tu yî gòr nè bsoogɛ̀ nà à ka' vʉ̂, m ka' teni wee mnsa' ca."
eng: But Felix, having more exact knowledge concerning the Way, deferred them, saying, When Lysias, the commanding officer, comes down, I will decide your case.

lmp: E m làa nè tu nè bsoogɛ̀ rjèe enɛ a ke'ni Pôl, a ker laa enɛ a kè'ni wa'a, a gee tɛ e ce koo mbɛp, ma'shi tɛ bkar vi a ce vʉ̀ ce jà' ye nè buu.
eng: He ordered the centurion that Paul should be kept in custody, and should have some privileges, and not to forbid any of his friends to serve him or to visit him.

lmp: Mnòŋ mo' vi ka' càa, Fɛlìs à vʉ a ŋgwa yì ce a m ce too enɛ Dusilɛ̀ ce à m ba muu Jûs. E tuu bèe, a vʉ nè Pôl, Pol à ka' vʉ̀ a suŋ àmbò rbyemî nè Jisos Krâis, e ce yu'shi.
eng: But after some days, Felix came with Drusilla, his wife, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.

lmp: Pol à ka' kɛ̀' ce suŋ àmbò ŋgêe yɛɛnì ba àmbò àde' ŋwɛ̀ kur ntee ker ba àmbò nòŋ mnsa' Nyʉ̀, Fɛlìs à wɛ̂p, a laa enɛ̂, "Wɛ̀ làa yi ghɛɛ sè'ni. Dù yo yu. M be koni fɛŋ tɛ m ka' kèr tuu bèe tɛ a vʉ nè wɛ̀."
eng: As he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was terrified, and answered, Go your way for this time, and when it is convenient for me, I will summon you.

lmp: E m ce kwà'shi foŋ enɛ Pol be yuni ye. E ka' ce kwà'shi wa'a, a ce kɛ' Pol àfo àfo a ce de' a ye.
eng: Meanwhile, he also hoped that money would be given to him by Paul, that he might release him. Therefore also he sent for him more often, and talked with him.

lmp: Bfè' vi ka' câa bbaa, Poshò Fɛstòs à lor dî' Fɛlìs, a ba à govanò. Fɛlìs à m ce kòŋ enɛ e gee tɛ nyor boŋ Jûs. E ka' kòŋ wa'a, a ku lɛ Pol mbe shaŋ.
eng: But when two years were fulfilled, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, and desiring to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul in bonds.

lmp: Mnòŋ vi ka' câa btaar, kɛ' embe nfè' ce Fɛstòs à m koo nta', Fɛstòs à natî à rla' Sisàriyà a du à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m.
eng: Festus therefore, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.

lmp: E ka' bà', bêe bgòrgòr efa mʉ̀ ŋgâa taŋshi taŋshì ba btu efa mʉ̀ Jus a vʉ̂, a yɛ ye a suŋ ye buu ce Pol à m gèe. Wowèe a m làa nè ye tatap
eng: Then the high priest and the principal men of the Jews informed him against Paul, and they begged him,

lmp: enɛ e gee yuu ce nyor boŋ wowèe, laa tɛ Pol vʉ à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m. Wowèe a m làa wa'a njobè' wowèe a m cu mncʉ̀ enɛ Pol à ka' ce vʉ̀, banɛ wowèe a be tɛ' à nduunjì, koo yʉ.
eng: asking a favor against him, that he would summon him to Jerusalem; plotting to kill him on the way.

lmp: Fɛstòs à beesì nè wowèe enɛ Pol yu à rla' Sisàriyà, bèe a ce kè'ni ye àfo, banɛ e be cu ba mnòŋ mʉcàr, kʉti à rla' anà.
eng: However Festus answered that Paul should be kept in custody at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to depart shortly.

lmp: E m làa nè wowèe enɛ a ma'shi tɛ a btu efa wâp mʉ a du à rla' Sisàriyà, ka' ba enɛ e gèe yuu mo' bebep, tɛ wowèe a bo làa yuu ce a tʉr à rlàa kuu ye.
eng: Let them therefore, said he, that are in power among you go down with me, and if there is anything wrong in the man, let them accuse him.

lmp: E ka' cu a wowèe àmbò mnòŋ waami kɛ̀ mnòŋ rʉʉ wa'a, a nati a du à rla' Sisàriyà. Tʉ̀' à ka' raa, e niŋ mbe kor à rsa' mnsa', a laa enɛ a vʉ nè Pôl.
eng: When he had stayed among them more than ten days, he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he sat on the judgment seat, and commanded Paul to be brought.

lmp: Pol à ka' vʉ̀, Jus ce a m vʉ̂ à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m nà a vʉ a tɛɛte, a sir ye a fa mbetar, a suŋ ku' buu ce e m gèe. Geewa'a yuu mo' yi m ba ce yi m ce dùŋshi enɛ buu anà à m ba mini ka'.
eng: When he had come, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing against him many and grievous charges which they could not prove,

lmp: Pol à kanì, a laa enɛ̂, "Mɛ̀ gèe fàa mò' kuu mncir Jûs, ba Ndap Nyʉ̀ ka', a gee fàa mò' nè ŋkʉʉ à to' Rum ka'."
eng: while he said in his defense, Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I sinned at all.

lmp: Fɛstòs à ka' ce kòŋ à rgèe tɛ nyor boŋ Jûs, e laa nè Pol enɛ̂, "Wɛ̀ kòŋ à rdù à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m tɛ m sa' wo mnsa' ca ba àfo a?"
eng: But Festus, desiring to gain favor with the Jews, answered Paul and said, Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem, and be judged by me there concerning these things?

lmp: Pol à beesì enɛ̂, "M tɛɛ sè'ni ba mbe kor ŋkwe Rûm, à ba mbe dì' ce a be sa' wa mnsa'. Mɛ̀ gèe fàa mò' nè Jus ka', wɛ wɛ̀ foŋ rìŋ wa'a.
eng: But Paul said, I am standing before Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you also know very well.

lmp: Ka' ba enɛ mɛ̀ bʉ' ncir a gee yuu mo' ce a ba yʉ mɛ̀, m kanì efa rkwe ka'. Ka' ba enɛ buu ce Jus a làa àmbò mɛ̀ na vi yu mini ka', ŋwɛ̀ mò' tʉr ŋger à rkoo mɛ̀ fa nè wowèe ka'. M ce kòŋ mɛnɛ a sa' wa mnsa' ba njeptii ŋkwe Rûm."
eng: For if I have done wrong, and have committed anything worthy of death, I don't refuse to die; but if none of those things is true that they accuse me of, no one can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar!

lmp: Fɛstòs à du a de' a yì bèe ce a m ce cep ye, a laa enɛ̂, "Wɛ̀ làa wɛnɛ ŋkwe Rum be sa' wo mnsa', banɛ a be dù yɛ ba ye."
eng: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you shall go.

lmp: Mnòŋ mo' vi ka' càa, ŋkʉʉ Agripà ba Bɛ̀nis a du à rla' Sisàriyà à rcà'ni Fɛstòs.
eng: Now when some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea, and greeted Festus.

lmp: Wowèe a ka' cu àfo à mʉ mnòŋ mo', Fɛstòs à suŋ mnsa' Pol nè ŋkʉʉ. E m suŋ ye enɛ̂, "Ŋwɛ̀ mò' yu àfa ce Fɛlìs à m ce dù, a lɛ àfa à ŋwɛ̀ shaŋ.
eng: As he stayed there many days, Festus laid Paul's case before the king, saying, There is a certain man left a prisoner by Felix;

lmp: Mɛ̀ ka' dù à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m, bêe bgòrgòr efa mʉ̀ ŋgâa taŋshi taŋshì ba bleebèe efa mʉ̀ Jus a suŋ buu ce e gèe, a laa enɛ m laa mɛnɛ e gwè mnsa'.
eng: about whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, asking for a sentence against him.

lmp: Mɛ̀ suŋ wowèe enɛ ndèe Rum yu enɛ a ka' vʉ nè ŋwɛ̀ ce e gèe fàa, banɛ bèe ce a làa enɛ e gèe fàa nà, a be vʉ̀, tɛ ye ye laa yuu kuu fàa ce a làa enɛ e gèe, tɛ a ka' teni mnsa'.
eng: To whom I answered that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man to destruction, before the accused has met the accusers face to face, and has had opportunity to make his defense concerning the matter laid against him.

lmp: Wèr wowèe à ka' vʉ̀ àfa, mɛ̀ caasì nfè' ka'. Tʉ̀' à ka' raa, mɛ̀ niŋ mbe kor à rsa' mnsa', a laa mɛnɛ a vʉ nè ŋwɛ̀ anà.
eng: When therefore they had come together here, I didn't delay, but on the next day sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought.

lmp: Bèe ce a m làa enɛ e gèe fàa nà a tɛɛ mbe kôr, a laa yuu mo' efa buu bbebep ce mɛ̀ m ce kwà'shi enɛ wowèe a be làa àmbò ye ka'.
eng: Concerning whom, when the accusers stood up, they brought no charge of such things as I supposed;

lmp: Yuu ce wowèe a m làa yi m ku ba ba àmbò mnsɛr ce a wowèe a m ce sɛr àmbò njɛ̀ɛ njì ce a wowèe a ke loo nè Nyʉ̀, ker ba foŋ àmbò ŋwɛ̀ mò' ce e m kwe, ce a m ce too enɛ Jisòs ce Pol à m ce làa enɛ e cu ntèe nà.
eng: but had certain questions against him about their own religion, and about one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

lmp: Mɛ̀ riŋ yuu ce àde' mɛ̀ m ba gee kuu yuu ce a m ce sɛr mnsɛr àtu mo nà ka'. Yi ka' ba wa'a, mɛ̀ laa nè ye mɛnɛ e be kòŋ à rdù à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m dù sa' vi mnsa' àfo lɛ?
eng: Being perplexed how to inquire concerning these things, I asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and there be judged concerning these matters.

lmp: Pol à laa enɛ a caasi vi mnsa' tɛ du teni ba Tàr Maŋgòŋ, mɛ̀ laa mɛnɛ a ku ce ke'ni ye caar tɛ nfè' ce m be tuusi ye nè ŋkwe Rum ka' ghɛɛ."
eng: But when Paul had appealed to be kept for the decision of the emperor, I commanded him to be kept until I could send him to Caesar.

lmp: Agripà à laa nè Fɛstòs enɛ̂, "M be kòŋ foŋ à ryu' yuu ce ŋwɛ̀ anà be làa." Fɛstòs à beesì enɛ̂, "À be yu' yuu ce e be làa ba àyàŋsè."
eng: Agrippa said to Festus, I also would like to hear the man myself. Tomorrow, he said, you shall hear him.

lmp: Tʉ̀' à ka' raa, Agripà ba Bɛ̀nis a vʉ nè fòo-ŋwɛ̀, a niŋ mbe ndàp rcutè. A m niŋ mbo a bèe ce a m ba btu nè bsoogɛ̀, ba bêe bgòrgôr à rla' ca. Fɛstòs à lâa, a vʉ nè Pôl.
eng: So on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp, and they had entered into the place of hearing with the commanding officers and principal men of the city, at the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.

lmp: A ka' vʉ̀ nè ye, e laa enɛ̂, "Ŋkʉʉ Agripà ker ba bèe wɛɛwɛ ce wèr wowèe yu tâa, yɛ nè ŋwɛ̀ ce Jus wɛɛwɛ a m tuu bèe enɛ a vʉ yɛ mɛ̀, suŋ buu ce e gèe. Wowèe a vʉ a yɛ mɛ̀ à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m, ker ba àfa, a ce waani, a ce làa enɛ e yu ŋwɛ̀ ce e ba kèr cu ntèe ka'.
eng: Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, you see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews petitioned me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

lmp: Mɛ̀ m fyɛ' a yɛ mɛnɛ e bʉ' ncir ka', a gee yuu mo' bebep ce àde' a m ba yʉ ye yʉ ka', à ka' ba njobè' e m kòŋ enɛ Tàr Maŋgòŋ sa' vi mnsa', mɛ̀ laa mɛnɛ m be tuusi ye nè ye.
eng: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and as he himself appealed to the emperor I determined to send him.

lmp: Ka' yi yu wa'a, mɛ̀ yɛ yuu mo' ce e gèe ce mɛ̀ ba saŋ suŋ Tata ka'. A mbùu ce mɛ̀ vʉ̀ nè ye njep wêe tìi, laŋlaŋ njeptii wɛ̀ ce ŋkʉʉ Agripà, tɛ sêe ce fyɛ' nje mʉ̀ mnsa' ca tɛ m bo tʉr yuu ce m saŋ.
eng: Of whom I have no certain thing to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him forth before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, that, after examination, I may have something to write.

lmp: Yi yu yɛɛnì enɛ m tuusi ŋwɛ̀ shaŋ ce mɛ̀ buu efa rsaŋ, suŋ yuu ce e gèe ka'."
eng: For it seems to me unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not to also specify the charges against him.

lmp: Agripà à laa nè Pol enɛ̂, "Mɛ̀ fa wɛ̀ njì enɛ à laa eku wɛ̂ cùu." Pol à naa bo mbekì a laa yuu. E m làa enɛ̂,
eng: Agrippa said to Paul, You may speak for yourself. Then Paul stretched out his hand, and made his defense.

lmp: "Ŋkʉʉ Agripà, mɛ̀ yɛ mɛnɛ mɛ̀ koni rbôŋtu ntìni na à rtɛɛ a wɛ̂ bsii làa yuu kuu buu wɛɛwɛ ce Jus a làa kuu mɛ̀.
eng: I think myself happy, King Agrippa, that I am to make my defense before you this day concerning all the things that I am accused by the Jews,

lmp: Wowèe a rìŋ mɛ̀ kɛ' ese à nfè' njìsàp sê. Wowèe a ka' koŋ à rlàa, àde' a ku laa enɛ mɛ̀ m ba mò' efa mʉ̀ bèe ce a ke gèe mcɛ̂r à njɛ̀ɛ njì ce a ke loo nè yàp Nyʉ̀ ka', a cu àmbò ŋwɛ̀ Farìsî.
eng: having known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that after the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

lmp: Mɛ̀ tɛɛ mbena sè'ni à mnsa' njobè' mɛ̀ byemi, a ce kè' buu ce Nyʉ̀ à m kà' nè visèe btâ,
eng: Now I stand here to be judged for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,

lmp: à ba buu ce visèe mntɛ̂' ncòp baa-à-rrʉ̀ʉ a ce loo nè Nyʉ̀ nètʉ' ba nèmootì, a ce kè' foŋ enɛ a be koni vi. Tàr Maŋgòŋ, yu njobè' rbyemì ca ce enɛ Jus a lòr mɛ̀ à mnsa'.
eng: which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa!

lmp: Yi yu tatap nè wèe à rbyemi enɛ Nyʉ̀ e ke fʉr bèe ce a kweŋger efa rkwe njokɛ?
eng: Why is it judged incredible with you, if God does raise the dead?

lmp: "Mɛ mɛ̀ foŋ à m kwà'shi mɛnɛ mɛ̀ ba gèe yuu wɛɛwɛ ce àde' m gêe, à rkani buu ce vi m ba kuu Jisòs à rla' Nasarɛ̀t.
eng: I myself most certainly thought that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

lmp: Tàr Maŋgòŋ, nyʉ̀ à ka' kùu ŋgòŋ, mɛ̀ yɛ àmbò rraa li raa embe bùu, mbe mɛ̂ ndù, ker ba à ndù bèe ce wèr wowèe à m ce dù. Rraa anà li m raa a caa nyʉ̀.
eng: at noon, O king, I saw on the way a light from the sky, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who traveled with me.

lmp: Wèr wɛɛwɛ à gweŋgèr à nshè, mɛ̀ yu' àmbò njèndoŋ ce làa nè mɛ̀ à li Hibrù enɛ̂, "Sôl, Sôl, À ce fa mɛ̀ ŋgɛ' njokɛ? Wɛ̀ ka' yɛ lùr ku tʉʉ kùu njo, banɛ yi be yaŋ ba wɛ̀."
eng: When we had all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.'

lmp: Mɛ̀ beesì mɛnɛ̂, "Tatâ, a wɛ̀ nda?" Tata à laa enɛ̂, "A mɛ̀ Jisòs ce à ce jar nè ye nà.
eng: I said, 'Who are you, Lord?' He said, 'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

lmp: Nàti tɛɛ mbekì, njobè' mɛ̀ vʉ̀ tɛ m bo ce wɛ̀ à yà ŋwɛ̀ rfà', ker ba à ŋwɛ̀ ce à be ce suŋ bèe buu ce wɛ̀ yɛ ese mɛ̀ ntìni na, ker ba vì ce m be lò dùŋshi wɛ̀.
eng: But arise, and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you a servant and a witness both of the things which you have seen, and of the things which I will reveal to you;

lmp: M be fʉr wɛ̀ embà mmbo bèe Isrɛ̀l, ba embà mmbo bèe enje jɛɛ.
eng: delivering you from the people, and from the Gentiles, to whom I send you,

lmp: M ce tuu wɛ̀ enɛ à du mʉ' map mmir, gee tɛ wowèe a fʉʉ efa tʉ̀'nji du à rraa, lo enjeptii Satàn du njeptii Nyʉ̀, tɛ a bo fòosi wowèe efa yàp buu bbebep, tɛ wowèe a koni dì' à mʉ̀ bèe ce Nyʉ̀ à gèe wowèe a ba brara njobè' wowèe a byemi nè mɛ̀ nà."
eng: to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive remission of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in me.'

lmp: "Yi ka' ba wa'a, ŋkʉʉ Agripà, mɛ̀ kani efa rgèe yuu ce Nyʉ̀ à m suŋ mɛ̀ à njɛ̀ɛ rlo mo' nà ka'.
eng: Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,

lmp: Pol à ka' ce làa buu ca à njɛ̂ɛ wa'a, Fɛstòs à waa, a laa enɛ̂, "Pôl, tu yi ce kar wɛ̀ embo! Ku' yo ŋwà' ce wɛ̀ yɛ'ni anà yi gèe wɛ̀ ce baa."
eng: As he thus made his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, you are crazy! Your great learning is driving you insane!

lmp: Pol à beesì enɛ̂, "Màsà Fɛstòs, tu yi ce kar mɛ̀ embo ka', buu ce m ce làa vi yu mini, a ba nè bfee-ŋwɛ̀.
eng: But he said, I am not crazy, most excellent Festus, but boldly declare words of truth and reasonableness.

lmp: Ŋkʉʉ rìŋ buu ca. M ka' ce làa nè ye m ker ce wɛp yuu mo' ka'. Mɛ̀ rìŋ nè mini-ŋwɛ̀ enɛ e mɛŋni mo' efa buu ca ka' njobè' a m gèe vi ba à bsʉ̀ti ka'.
eng: For the king knows of these things, to whom also I speak freely. For I am persuaded that none of these things is hidden from him, for this has not been done in a corner.

lmp: Ŋkʉʉ Agripà, wɛ̀ byemi yuu ce ŋgâa ncep ntuu Nyʉ̀ a m làa a? Mɛ̀ rìŋ mɛnɛ wɛ̀ byemi."
eng: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.

lmp: Agripà à laa nè Pol enɛ̂, "Â kwà'shi enɛ àde' à ku lor nfè' mʉcàcàr wa'a, gee m ba ŋwɛ̀ rbyemì a?"
eng: Agrippa said to Paul, With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?

lmp: Pol à laa enɛ̂, "Kɛ̀ yu nfè' yî mʉcàr ɛ̀, kɛ̀ yu yî njìsàp ɛ̀, m ce loo nè Nyʉ̀ mɛnɛ wɛ̀ ker ba bèe wɛɛwɛ ce a ce yu' yuu ce m ce làa ntìni na, a ba ba àmbò mɛ mɛ̀ yu na, ke' ba ŋgâa shaŋ foŋ àmbò mɛ̀ ka'."
eng: Paul said, I pray to God, that whether with little or with much, not only you, but also all that hear me this day, might become such as I am, except for these bonds.

lmp: Ŋkʉʉ ba govanò ba Bɛ̀nîs, ker ba bɛr bèe wɛɛwɛ a natì mbekì.
eng: The king rose up with the governor, and Bernice, and those who sat with them.

lmp: A ka' nàti dù, a sèesî, a laa enɛ̂, "Ŋwɛ̀ ca ce gèe yuu mo' ce àde' a ba yʉ ye kɛ̀ fa ye à shaŋ ka'."
eng: When they had withdrawn, they spoke one to another, saying, This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.

lmp: Agripà à laa nè Fɛstòs enɛ̂, "Ŋwɛ̀ ca à ka' tɛ bà làa enɛ ŋkwe Rum a ŋwɛ̀ ce e be sa' vi mnsa' ka', sèe à ba mà'shi ye tɛ e dû."
eng: Agrippa said to Festus, This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.

lmp: A ka' sèesi enɛ wèr Pol wèe be niŋ mbe keŋ ŋgòr dù à to' Italè, a lor Pol ba ŋgâa shaŋ mo' a fa nè tu nè bsoogɛ̀ rjèe efa bkʉr bsoogɛ̀ ŋkwe Rûm. A m ce too ŋwɛ̀ ca enɛ Julìyòs.
eng: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.

lmp: Wèr à m niŋ mbe keŋ ŋgòr ce à m ba yî à dì' ce a m ce too enɛ Àdamitùm. Keŋ anà à m tɛɛ à rco'ti dù, ce tɛɛtɛ à mla' mô' àwâa rò à ŋgôŋ Ɛshà. Wèr à niŋ mbo a ce dù. Àristakòs ce à m ba ŋwɛ̂ à rla' Tɛ̀sàlonikâ à ŋgôŋ Mɛ̀sɛ̀donìyà à m ba wèr wowèe.
eng: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea; Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

lmp: Tʉ̀' à ka' raa, wèr à ba' à rla' Sidòn. Julìyòs à gee ŋgêe bòŋboŋ nè Pôl. E m mà'shi ye e du a yɛ bkar vi tɛ wowèe a bo kè' à ye.
eng: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly, and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.

lmp: Wèr à lô àfo a niŋ mbe keŋ a ce dù, fu' yi ka' ce vʉ̂ à mbèp ce keŋ à m ce dù, wèr à lɛ' à mbèp mô' à ŋgôŋ Saipròs ce fu' yi m ce càa ka'.
eng: Putting to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

lmp: Wèr à ka' tuu rô à ŋgôŋ Sìlesìyà ba à ŋgôŋ Pàmfilìyà a du a ba' à rla' Mirà à ŋgôŋ Lishà.
eng: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

lmp: Wèr à ka' bà' àfo, tu nè bsoogɛ̀ rjèe yi yɛ keŋ yî à rla' Àlɛ̀ksandà ce e m ce dù à to' Italè, a fa wèr mbo.
eng: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, and he put us on board.

lmp: Wèr à m ce dù mʉwɛ̀ɛ-mʉwɛ̀ɛ, a lor mnòŋ àŋgoo, a yɛ ŋgɛ' sê, a ka' ba' àtʉtʉ rla' Kidòm. Fu' yi m mà'shi enɛ wèr ba' à rla' anà ka', wèr à lɛ' a du à mbèp mô' àgee to' Krêt ce fu' yi m ce càa ka'. Rla' Sàlmonè li ba yi nje yɛɛ.
eng: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

lmp: Keŋ à ce dii àwâa rò, wèr à yɛ ŋgɛ' sê, a ka' ba' à dì' ce a m ce too enɛ Fɛɛ Hɛvɛ̀n àgee rla' Lisìyà.
eng: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.

lmp: Wèr à m càasi nfè' à nduunjì gòr sê. Rjɛ̀r li m ba nè mlù-ŋwɛ̀ sê, njobè' nòŋ ce a ke taŋshi taŋshî gòr yi m càa, à m ba à cùu saa.
eng: When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous, because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished them,

lmp: Yi ka' ba wa'a, Pol à bɛɛ wowèe a laa enɛ̂, "Bèe câ, mɛ̀ yɛ mɛnɛ lisèe rjɛ̀r ca li be ba yɛɛnì ka'. Sèe ka' lô àfa banɛ yìsèe buu be bep, tɛ keŋ bep, tɛ bèe a kweŋger foŋ."
eng: and said to them, Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.

lmp: Geewa'a, tu nè bsoogɛ̀ rjèe yi m byemi ba yuu ce ŋwɛ̀ ce e m ce dòo keŋ ker ba ŋwɛ̀ ce e m tʉr keŋ anà a m làa.
eng: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to those things which were spoken by Paul.

lmp: Dì' ce wowèe a m vʉ̀ tɛɛ àfo anà à m ba dî' bòŋboŋ à rcu à saa ka'. Bèe magòr a fa ntaŋ enɛ a gheter yɛ enɛ a be bà' à rla' Fenìs cu ba àfo lɛ. Fenìs à m ba dì' mô' à to' Krêt ce bkeŋ vi m ce vʉ̀ ce tɛɛ, ka' ker ce co'ti ce dù. À m ba dì' ce wɛ̀ m ka' ba tɛɛ ce kè' mbà mbùuntii, à ku yɛ rdip à yo bo ŋkòp ba yo bo mà'.
eng: Because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised going to sea from there, if by any means they could reach Phoenix, and winter there, which is a port of Crete, looking northeast and southeast.

lmp: Mʉ fu' mo' yi ce vʉ̀ embà mbùuŋgòŋ, wowèe a kwa'shì enɛ a koni yuu ce a ce ròo. Wowèe a sʉŋ ma co' ce keŋ à m tɛɛ àgho a lɛ mbe keŋ a co'ti a ce dù àwâa rô à to' Krêt.
eng: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.

lmp: Wowèe a m dù njìsàp ka', ma ntèendʉŋ mò' à sûu à to' Krêt, à ba yì ce a too enɛ̂, Yî à bke'.
eng: But before long, a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.

lmp: Ntèendʉŋ anà à koo à keŋ, keŋ à moo à rdù làr, wèr à boŋlàr a ma'shî, e lor keŋ a ce dù àgho.
eng: When the ship was caught, and couldn't face the wind, we gave way to it, and were driven along.

lmp: Wèr à caa a du à ŋgʉ̀' mô' à rla' Kàwudà ce fu' yi m ce càa ka', a gheter sê, tɛ keŋ ŋkɛ' ce a m cʉʉ mbà mbùu yî ŋgòr anà ka' bep ka'.
eng: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.

lmp: A m sʉ̀ŋ a niŋ àgho mbe mʉ̀ yî ŋgòr, a fyɛɛ bkʉ̀ a kur keŋ ŋgòr àgho fà dì' e sa'ŋger ka'. Wowèe a ka' ce wɛp enɛ keŋ be bà' Sitì, niŋ njep mʉ̀ nsaruŋ tɛɛ, wowèe a suusì ma co' ce keŋ à m ce tɛɛ àgho nà njep mʉ̀ rò tɛ keŋ bo tɛɛ, keŋ à ku ce dù nè yi bo.
eng: After they had hoisted it up, they used cables to help reinforce the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars, they lowered the sea anchor, and so were driven along.

lmp: Ntèendʉŋ ca à ku ce càa, a ce fa wèr ŋgɛ' sê. Tʉ̀' à ka' raa, wowèe a kɛ' a ce fʉshi buu embe keŋ a ce mà'ri njep rò.
eng: As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.

lmp: Mnòŋ vi ka' bâ' btaar, wowèe a lor buu mfà' embe keŋ nè map mmbo, a ma'ri njep rò.
eng: On the third day, they threw out the ship's tackle with their own hands.

lmp: Mnòŋ vi m càa àŋgoo sê, wèr à be yɛ rlir nyʉ̀ kɛ̀ mkàŋsì ka', ntèendʉŋ à ku ce càa tatap sê. Wèr à riŋ enɛ àde' wèr luŋ efa gho ka'.
eng: When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days, and no small storm pressed on us, all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.

lmp: Bèe ca a ka' cu tètè sê, ye yuu ka', Pol à natì a tɛɛ a wâp mʉ a laa enɛ̂, "Bèe câ, wèe à mʉ yu' yuu ce mɛ̀ mʉ laa nè wèe à to' Krêt nà, cu àfo, yìsèe buu à ba kèr bep, bʉ à cicì ka'.
eng: When they had been long without food, Paul stood up in the middle of them, and said, Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete, and have gotten this injury and loss.

lmp: M ce làa nè wèe sè'ni na enɛ wèe kur ntee. Mò' efa wèe be kwe ka'. Yuu ce yi be bep, sà'ŋger, ku ba keŋ cà'cà'.
eng: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.

lmp: À ba nètʉ', Nyʉ̀ ce e tʉr mɛ̀, ce mɛ̂ ke loo nè ye, à tuusì yì ncìndap, e vʉ a tɛɛ a mɛ̂ geŋ,
eng: For there stood by me this night an angel, belonging to the God whose I am and whom I serve,

lmp: a laa enɛ̂, "Pôl, fa wɛp ka'. À be kù tɛɛ à bsii Sisà. Nyʉ̀ à tʉr wɛ̀ à ntee bòŋboŋ, a ja' myôŋ bèe ce wèe wowèe yu mbe keŋ na njo' wɛ̀."
eng: saying, 'Don't be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. Behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.'

lmp: Bèe câ, banɛ wèe kur ntee njobè' mɛ̀ byemi mɛnɛ yi be kù ba àmbò Nyʉ̀ à làa nè mɛ̀.
eng: Therefore, sirs, cheer up! For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.

lmp: Geewa'a, keŋ be niŋ nje mʉ̀ nsaruŋ, tàŋte, tɛɛ àwâa rla' mo'."
eng: But we must run aground on a certain island.

lmp: À ka' ba nètʉ' ce mnòŋ vi bà' war ncòp-kyèe-à-rrʉ̀ʉ, ntèendʉŋ à ku ce dà' nè wèr à rdip ce a m ce too enɛ Ànduyà. À ba àmbò nè ntee tʉ' wa'a, bèe ce a m ce dòo keŋ a yu' enjep blɛɛ enɛ wowèe a ce bà' àwâa rò.
eng: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.

lmp: Wowèe a lor kʉ̀, a cʉʉ yuu rìr rir à cùu efa gho, a suusi njep rò a yɛ enɛ rcoomì efa rdip anà li yu àmbò mkoo mbaa. A ka' kèr dù mʉ ntàm mò', a ker suusi kʉ̀ anà njo a yɛ enɛ rcoomì efa gho li yu mkoo ncòp-ta-à-rrʉ̀ʉ.
eng: They took soundings, and found twenty fathoms. After a little while, they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.

lmp: Wowèe a wɛp enɛ keŋ be kùu nyor à blùr njep mʉ̀ rò, a lor bco' ce keŋ e ke tɛɛ àgho njep mʉ̀ rò nà embà mbùu keŋ vi kyèe, a fa njep rò, a loo enɛ tʉ̀' raa cɛrcɛr.
eng: Fearing that we would run aground on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for daylight.

lmp: Bèe ce a m ce dòo keŋ ca a ghetèr enɛ a ba caŋ fʉʉ embo, a lor keŋ ŋkɛ' a suusi njep rò, a bo'shi enɛ wowèe a ce dù kù cûu keŋ tɛ a bo kèr fʉr bco' mo' ce keŋ e ke tɛɛ àgho njep rò nà.
eng: As the sailors were trying to flee out of the ship, and had lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they would lay out anchors from the bow,

lmp: Pol à laa nè tu nè bsoogɛ̀ rjèe ba bsoogɛ̀ enɛ̂, "Bèe ca a ka' tɛ kù cu mbe keŋ na ka', wèe luŋ ka'."
eng: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Unless these stay in the ship, you can't be saved.

lmp: Bsoogɛ̀ a ceeshì bkʉ̀ efa keŋ ŋkɛ', e ce dù mbà rò.
eng: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat, and let it fall off.

lmp: Tʉ̀' à ka' kɛ̀' ce raa, Pol à bu' mmbo nè wowèe wɛɛwɛ enɛ wowèe a ye yuu. E m làa nè wowèe enɛ̂, "Wèe à yɛ mlù, a cu nè njè à mnòŋ ncòp-kyèe-à-rrʉ̀ʉ, a joo yuu kù cùu ka'.
eng: While the day was coming on, Paul begged them all to take some food, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that you wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.

lmp: Banɛ m ce bu' mmbo nè wèe enɛ wèe ye yuu. Wèe à ka' tɛ ye yuu ka', wèe luŋ ka'. Mbʉ̀ nyʉ̀'tu embe tu ŋwɛ̀ mò' efa wêe mʉ be dù à yuu ka'."
eng: Therefore I beg you to take some food, for this is for your safety; for not a hair will perish from any of your heads.

lmp: Pol à ka' làa buu ca nè wowèe mìsi, a lor brɛ̂d, a loo a yoŋshi Nyʉ̀ à wâp bsii, a bɛ' a kɛ' a ce ye.
eng: When he had said this, and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all, and he broke it, and began to eat.

lmp: Ca yi m fa wowèe ŋger, wowèe a wasè, a ye yuu.
eng: Then they all cheered up, and they also took food.

lmp: Wèr à m ba mbe keŋ anà wɛɛwɛ bèe mjêe mbaa nè ncòp-ntuunfu-à- mnsàambâ.
eng: In all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.

lmp: Wowèe a ka' ye byee yu' bòŋboŋ, a fʉshi msaŋ ce mi m ba mbe keŋ a ma' njep rò tɛ keŋ bo fɛp.
eng: When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.

lmp: Tʉ̀' à ka' raa, wowèe a yɛ nje waa ŋkʉ̀, a riŋ fàdì' ce wowèe a m ba anà ka', a ka' ce fyɛ', a yɛ dì' mo' ce rdip li tuŋ a bɛrsî, nsaruŋ à ba àwâa rò anà sê. Wowèe a kwa'shi enɛ yi ka' ba àtɛ̀r wowèe a doo keŋ anà du àgho mbe dì' anà, tɛ e bo niŋ njep mʉ̀ nsaruŋ tɛɛ.
eng: When it was day, they didn't recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, and they decided to try to drive the ship onto it.

lmp: Wowèe a ceeshì bco' ce keŋ e ke tɛɛ àgho njep mʉ̀ rò, vi suu njep rò, a ker ba'shi bkʉ̀ ce a ke kur yuu ce a ke dòo keŋ àgho. Wowèe a ka' gèe wa' mìsi, a naa ma cɛ̂' bɛ̀bɛr ce yi m ba kù cûu keŋ tɛ fu' yi bo koo njo, dòo keŋ dù àgho.
eng: Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time untying the rudder ropes. Hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.

lmp: Geewa'a, keŋ à niŋ njep mʉ̀ nsaruŋ yì embe dì' ce mdip mi m ce tarte a mmo', a tɛɛ. Cûu keŋ yi niŋ njep mʉ̀ nsaruŋ anà bòŋboŋ sê, a taŋte njo. Mdip ce mi m ce baŋti ce vʉ̀ nè ŋger-ŋwɛ̀ se nà, mi sa'sì mbùu keŋ.
eng: But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground. The bow struck and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.

lmp: Bsoogɛ̀ a fa ntaŋ enɛ a be yʉshi ŋgâa shaŋ ce a m ba mbe keŋ anà wɛɛwɛ fà dì' mò' efa wowèe bo coo njep rò bu' rdip, fʉʉ nje waa ŋkʉ̀ caŋ ka'.
eng: The soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim out and escape.

lmp: Tu nè bsoogɛ̀ rjèe yi m ce kòŋ à rjà' Pol efa rkwe, a kani wowèe efa ryʉshi ŋgâa shaŋ. E m làa enɛ bèe ce a rìŋ à rbu' rdip a nyɛɛ coo njep rò entombì bu' rdip, du nje waa ŋkʉ̀.
eng: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should throw themselves overboard first to go toward the land;

lmp: Yi m ba enɛ bɛr bèe mo' a ba'ni plâŋ, tɛ bɛr mo' a ba'ni bbàbàr keŋ ce e m sà'ŋger nà. A m gèe wa'a, wèr wowèe wɛɛwɛ à du a ba' nje waa ŋkʉ̀, yuu mo' yi joo ŋwɛ̀ mò' ka'.
eng: and the rest should follow, some on planks, and some on other things from the ship. So it happened that they all escaped safely to the land.

lmp: Wèr à ka' bà' nje waa ŋkʉ̀, lùŋ efa ŋgɛ', a yu' enɛ rlii rla' ce rdip li m sìr a tarte anà li yu enɛ Mɛlità.
eng: When we had escaped, then they learned that the island was called Malta.

lmp: Bêe à rla' anà a m gèe ŋgêe bòŋboŋ nè wèr, a caa embe dì' ce wèr à m ce kwà'shi. Wowèe a m koni wèr, a too mor njobè' mbèŋ à m ce gwè, mbɛp à ce fʉte.
eng: The natives showed us uncommon kindness; for they kindled a fire, and received us all, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

lmp: Pol à baashì ŋguu a byɛ' mbe rkoo, a ka' ce tòo, nyo à fʉʉ enjo njobè' mor yi m lùu gòr, a luu ye à bò, a barni àgho.
eng: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

lmp: Bêe à rla' anà a ka' yɛ àmbò nyo ce lɛŋlɛŋ ye à bò, wowèe a laa fa wâp mʉ enɛ̂, "Ŋwɛ̀ anà ku ba ŋwɛ̀ ce e yʉ ŋwɛ̀. Ka' e lùŋ efa rkwe enjep rò wa'a, e ku bii nyàa rkwe."
eng: When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said one to another, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped from the sea, yet Justice has not allowed to live.

lmp: Pol à kar nyo ca efa bò, e gwe njep mor, yuu mo' yi gee ye ka'.
eng: However he shook off the creature into the fire, and wasn't harmed.

lmp: Wowèe a m ce kè' enɛ bo yi ka' tɛ kù ko' ye mbe dì' ka', banɛ e be kù lò co'ti gwè à nshè, kwe. Wowèe a cu nfè' njìsàp sê, a yɛ yuu mo' yi gee ye ka', wowèe a kupsè map mkwà'shì a laa enɛ̂, "E yu nyʉ̀ mò'."
eng: But they expected that he would have swollen or fallen down dead suddenly, but when they watched for a long time and saw nothing bad happen to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

lmp: Ŋwɛ̂ ŋgôr à rla' anà à m tʉr ŋkʉ̀ àtʉtʉ. A m ce too ye enɛ Pùbilìyòs. E m koni wèr, a nyaŋ wèr bòŋboŋ se à mnôŋ btaar.
eng: Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us, and courteously entertained us for three days.

lmp: Yì ta à m nòŋ a ce yaŋ. Mbɛp à m ce fʉte ye, e ker ce to' a ce fìŋshi. Pol à niŋ mbe dì' e m nòŋ, a gee rloo, a lɛ mmbo mbe yê ndù, e ke'sè.
eng: It happened that the father of Publius lay sick of fever and dysentery. Paul entered in to him, prayed, and laying his hands on him, healed him.

lmp: Ca yi ka' koni wa'a, bɛr ŋgâa byaŋ ce a m ba à rla' anà a vʉsè, Pol à gee wowèe a ke'sè.
eng: Then when this was done, the rest also who had diseases in the island came, and were cured.

lmp: Wowèe a m nàa wèr à mnduunjî jɛɛ jɛ̀ɛ jɛɛ. Wèr à ka' niŋ mbe keŋ tɛ wèr bo ce dù, wowèe a fa wèr buu ce vi bo jà' wèr.
eng: They also honored us with many honors, and when we sailed, they put on board the things that we needed.

lmp: Wèr à m cu à rla' ca à mŋwɛɛ btaar a ka' co'ti a ce dù mbe keŋ yî à rla' Àlɛ̀ksandà ce a m ce too enɛ Mfar Mnyʉ̀. E m tɛɛ à rla' ca njep mʉ̀ rò kɛ̂' à cùu saa caar saa à mî.
eng: After three months, we set sail in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island, whose sign was The Twin Brothers.

lmp: Wèr à du a ba' à rla' Sìrakusà a cu àfo mnôŋ btaar.
eng: Touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

lmp: Wèr à ka' lô àfo a kaari a ba' à rla' Rɛgìyòm. Tʉ̀' à ka' raa, fu' yi kɛ' a ce vʉ̀ embà mbùuŋgòŋ. Tʉ̀' mò' à ka' raa, wèr à ba' à rla' Pùtolì.
eng: From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,

lmp: Wèr à m yɛ bfʉr mo' àfo, wowèe a laa enɛ wèr wowèe cu àfo à mnòŋ sàambâ. Awɛ wèr à du a ba' à rla' Rûm.
eng: where we found brothers, and were entreated to stay with them for seven days. So we came to Rome.

lmp: Tɛ wèr ka' bà' à rla' Rûm, bfʉr ce à rla' anà a m banì yu' enɛ wèr yu à nduunjì. Wowèe a vʉ caar a ba' à ntaa yî à rla' Àpiyò, bèe mo' a ba' fàdì' bhòtɛl vi m ba vi btaar, tɛ a bo koni wèr. Pol à ka' yɛ wowèe, a yoŋshi Nyʉ̀, ŋger yi vʉ ye nje nyòr.
eng: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God, and took courage.

lmp: Wèr à ka' bà' à rla' Rûm, a ma'shi Pôl, e ce cu nè yi tu, ŋwɛ̀ soogɛ̀ mò' à ce kè'ni ye.
eng: When we entered into Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.

lmp: Mnòŋ vi ka' câa btaar, e kɛ' bêe bgòrgòr efa mʉ̀ Jus ce à rla' Rûm. Wowèe a ka' vʉ̀, e laa nè wowèe enɛ̂, "Yà bèe, ka' mɛ̀ m gèe fàa mò' nè yìsèe bèe kɛ̀ ma' ndèe to' ce visèe btarkʉ a m lɛ̀ nè sèe nà ka' wa'a, a ku koo mɛ̀ à rla' Jɛ̀rusalɛ̀m, a fa mbe mmbo bèe ŋkwe Rûm.
eng: It happened that after three days Paul called together those who were the leaders of the Jews. When they had come together, he said to them, I, brothers, though I had done nothing against the people, or the customs of our fathers, still was delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,

lmp: Bèe ŋkwe Rum ca a m bipshi buu nè mɛ̀, a koŋ à rmà'shi mɛ̀ njobè' mɛ̀ m gèe yuu mo' ce a m ba yʉ mɛ̀ àtu mo ka'.
eng: who, when they had examined me, desired to set me free, because there was no cause of death in me.

lmp: Geewa'a, Jus a ka' kani enɛ a fa mà'shi mɛ̀ ka', mɛ̀ boŋlàr a laa mɛnɛ wa mnsa' be sa' ŋkwe Rûm. Mɛ̀ m làa wa'a, a ke' tʉr yuu bebep mo' à rlàa kuu yà bèe ka'.
eng: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything about which to accuse my nation.

lmp: A mbùu ce mɛ̀ làa mɛnɛ wèe vʉ̂, tɛ m yɛ wèe, tɛ sèe de'. Kwàŋ yu mɛ̀ kù rkoo sè'ni na ba àtu ŋwɛ̀ ce bèe Isrɛ̀l a m cu a ce kè'."
eng: For this cause therefore I asked to see you and to speak with you. For because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.

lmp: Wowèe a beesì enɛ̂, "Wèr à be koo mŋwà' mô' à ŋgôŋ Jùdiyà ce a saŋ a kuu wɛ̀ ka'. Nfʉr yìsèe mò' à be vʉ̂ àfo nè nsuŋ mô' mbembep kɛ̀ a laa yuu bebep mo' kuu wɛ̀ ka'.
eng: They said to him, We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor did any of the brothers come here and report or speak any evil of you.

lmp: Ka' yi yu wa'a, wèr ce kòŋ à rrìŋ yuu ce à ce kwà'shi njobè' wèr rìŋ wernɛ bèe wɛɛwɛ a ce làa bebep kuu njɛ̀ɛ nduunjì ce à yu njo na."
eng: But we desire to hear from you what you think. For, as concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.

lmp: A Pol wèe a seesì a lɛ nòŋ ce wowèe a be vʉ̀ yɛ ye. Nòŋ anà yi ka' ghɛɛ, wowèe a vʉ sê, a caa àmbò wowèe a m ba nà, a yɛ Pol mbe dì' ce e m ce cu. E m suŋ wowèe àmbò kʉʉ Nyʉ̀, a nashi buu ca nè wowèe kɛ̂' à ŋgàptʉ' du ba' à mbùuŋkùr. E m ghèter à rgèe tɛ wowèe a byemi nè Jisòs, a ce fyɛ' mbe mŋwâ' mncir Musìs, ba mŋwâ' ŋgâa ncep ntuu Nyʉ̀ à rdùŋshi enɛ Jisòs yu Krâis anà.
